body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=080326_2&amount=25]
Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list -- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote.

With just one point separating me and working Texans from Abbott and his billionaire donors, the momentum in this race is undeniable.
I am fighting to end the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax that means we pay more and get less, by putting money back in your pocket. I am fighting to invest in our neighborhood schools and end Abbott's one billion dollar school voucher scam. I am fighting to end the data center madness that is hurting our communities and driving up our bills. And Texans are taking notice.
**A one-point poll like this only happens because Texans know this is our opportunity for real change.**
Texans are fed up with being last on Abbott's list, but we have a long way to go between now and Election Day. Your support has never been more important to keeping us on the road traveling to every corner of Texas and meeting with voters where they are.

# Monday, August 3, 2026
---
| Estimated Read Time: 3 MinutesJust The TruthYour No-BS NewsletterDear Readers,Today's sponsor, Turning Point USA, is supporting ballot-chasing efforts in Arizona and is asking supporters to help fund grassroots outreach ahead of the state's upcoming election.Thank you for your consideration of our sponsors.
The Just The Truth Team[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001._iltqNytX8R9_iqLaPZU6_It_HwwR2kK3CjKeiy9qBMIexGvCTMM1I5VQocm5cOMs38sHLEn1BD1LBmi64Y8QX8TQ68A9atMX0YGXiShT46XnFZbGnZUIT3P0bVIKw2gh04RfW9BLUSexzekNQimwMEYLnam2pXOu0JaUriSNhYOSLn2x6T6xFcSrqz2rSHCi5PgpuMBXj9cHX9TssfoOw/4sv/-BakyUgZQ9GTYoZTEYDbsw/h1/h001.W6shv4cFc63TiBc_bd9dtI4HU_BHivOQyEoWkdcYACU)Friend,In just a moment, we are going to ask you to fund our ballot chasers in Arizona. Please give us a chance to explain why this request – _especially today_ – is so important.Here is the truth:Arizona's primary election is July 21st. Early voting is already underway, and every single day between now and then matters. _We have to get our ballot chasers in front of voters right now, while there's still time to make a difference._ Now here is why this actually matters:**Arizona isn't just another swing state. It's the single most important state on the map.** The state carries 11 electoral votes, soon to be 12, and without winning it, most of the realistic paths to the White House disappear. **On Tuesday morning at 9:30 am ET, we 'll be hosting our regular livestream on YouTube and Twitter.** Then on **Tuesday evening at 7:30 pm ET we 'll go live** with Krystal Ball at both the [Drop Site](https://substack.com/redirect/e7e1eaf3-255f-4af2-80eb-f37c5ecc58bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Breaking Points](https://substack.com/redirect/321e0d28-d271-4c9e-8ef3-062ceb1a3847?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) YouTube pages, and we'll track the results until we have a winner. We'll have a number of interesting guests coming through, though I don't want to make any promises, because election nights can be chaotic. Tune in if you can. U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens hosts a campaign event with former House Majority Whip Congressman Jim Clyburn (left) and Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer (right) at Michigan Conference-Teamsters on July 24, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. Photo by Bill Pugliano/Getty Images.
_Story by Tom Perkins_
More than a dozen anti-establishment candidates running on populist economics and Israel policy are threatening to take seats now held by Democrats across Michigan, from U.S. Senate to city councils.
A sweep or strong showing by these insurgents in Tuesday's primary would be seismic, upending Democratic Party power dynamics in an establishment stronghold. More broadly, if the Democratic Tea Party comes for the bellwether state of Michigan, the results would show that a new bottom-up politics is taking root, providing the clearest signal yet that the fundamental shift in the party underway is not restricted to New York or heavily blue cities.
(A full list of the races to watch on Tuesday, plus a handful already concluded, is at the end of this story.)
To understand the moment here, one needs to look at the night of November 8, 2022, when midterm returns trickling in across Michigan slowly began to reveal a surprise result: Democrats had won a trifecta and [gained control over the state government](https://substack.com/redirect/5285985b-2cf8-47a5-87e4-0189fd24785b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the first time in 40 years.
To many in the party, it felt like the state was emerging from the darkness after decades of being unable to legislate under one of the nation's [most gerrymandered maps](https://substack.com/redirect/43a82af4-8fec-49ba-9c2b-8a28e5973f16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), suffering under GOP governors like Rick Snyder, architect of the Flint water crisis.
This kind of coverage matters. Make sure we can keep doing it:
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.KcZ6DtUQuIzqad6uAoimMii7Ry8x_44rA5k2pQWewm4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=209680937)
Rank-and-file Democrats expected that wildly popular proposals they supported would move easily into policy: making corporations pay for pollution, taxing the wealthy, dramatically expanding healthcare, addressing the soaring cost-of-living for the working class, and reining in DTE Energy, among the nation's most expensive and unreliable utilities.
These proposals did not pass. Most of the economic agenda died. No one was held responsible for Flint.
Pro-business Democrats in [leadership positions](https://substack.com/redirect/474d5377-13a9-4fe5-8b89-59553fbdd55d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including Gov. [Gretchen Whitmer,](https://substack.com/redirect/bd589338-964e-47bf-aeda-c03d0beecdac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [thwarted the most meaningful proposals](https://substack.com/redirect/474d5377-13a9-4fe5-8b89-59553fbdd55d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) while cutting the [Covid safety net](https://substack.com/redirect/e0327946-ae6d-444a-aa19-cd67ffe4fd78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The largely [squandered trifecta](https://substack.com/redirect/8ea4fc71-cb95-479f-934e-c9ac37d50f9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [failure](https://substack.com/redirect/25bfc5f9-32a8-4842-888b-b201d5705d2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to address Michigan's most urgent economic needs infuriated the base.
The party's failures to enact popular legislation dovetailed with outrage over the establishment's [attacks](https://substack.com/redirect/c948da6a-ce98-4350-9810-e44ff0b3cd58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on [pro-Palestinian advocates](https://substack.com/redirect/8fbfee17-c1e6-41a2-abec-de3af88e14c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [disrespect of](https://substack.com/redirect/b7181151-0ab9-4d14-852f-2741063ff606?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Michigan's huge Arab-American populations; centrist Democratic support for an onslaught of data center plans in the state; and the relentless prioritization of corporate interests over residents' needs. The state's powerful unions began inching away from corporate Democrats.
This confluence of forces ignited the groundswell of support for the 15 grassroots change candidates now on the ballot. Some have already won this cycle, and the rest may make major gains on Tuesday.
**Yousef Rabhi** is a Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) member aiming to unseat a 12-year party machine mayor in Ann Arbor, the state's most liberal big city. He is up 13 points per [a late July poll](https://substack.com/redirect/64fed59e-e783-4caa-b1b6-ad3819e450f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
"Ultimately a lot of the major landmark legislation that they promised just did not get delivered," he told Drop Site. "Now there's this combination of rank-and-file working people, progressive activists and folks from all over the political spectrum, people from Black, Arab, Jewish communities, who are feeling overlooked by Democratic party right now, and there is surge surge of left candidates where there is disaffection."
In the race for U.S. Senate, the latest polls put former Detroit health department director **Abdul El-Sayed** up by 10-15 points over Rep. **Haley Stevens** despite at least $30 million in spending by pro-Israel groups. The Bernie Sanders-endorsed, former Sunrise co-founder **William Lawrence** is up 15-25 points in a mid-Michigan U.S. House seat, though establishment polling has him behind. **Donovan McKinney** , backed by Justice Democrats and Sanders, was running slightly behind the AIPAC-backed incumbent Shri Thanedar in a poll on the Detroit U.S. House district race.
Downballot, former Uncommitted Movement co-founder and Sanders endorsee **Abbas Alawieh** is attempting to be the first Arab-American to serve in the state senate, and to represent Dearborn, a city with a huge Lebanese-American population. Alawieh previously served as a congressional aide to Reps. **Andy Levin** and **Rashida Tlaib** of Michigan, as well as **Cori Bush** -- who is mounting her own comeback bid in St. Louis on Tuesday. In a Detroit state house district, **Chris Gilmer-Hill** , backed by the DSA and Working Families Party, is running against State Rep. **Helena Scott** , a pugnacious machine politician.
But the insurgents face headwinds. The congressional races are awash in corporate and pro-Israel lobby money. Pro-Israel donors [are opposing](https://substack.com/redirect/52b535c4-700b-459a-b705-e423965f1132?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) leftist Yemeni-American state Senate candidate **Abe Aiyash** , and they account for about one-third of the $353,000 raised by his opponent, the establishment-backed **Justin Onwenu**.
Meanwhile, many older, [conservative black voters here](https://substack.com/redirect/51f879ac-424c-49cd-b75d-a8fb2a61c860?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have rejected Sanders-style politics, and division exists among them and Arab-Americans. The left has also been so weak in Michigan that there is little infrastructure like that which the DSA and Working Families Party laid for many years in New York that was essential to Zohran Mamdani's win, and the June "socialist sweep."
Still, the Working Families Party and DSA are [both gaining strength](https://substack.com/redirect/42ba9565-e89b-4e6d-9212-4933aed983ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and active this cycle. And there may be an "Abdul effect," said Bernie Porn, a state pollster with EPIC-MRA: "El-Sayed's strength will probably translate into strength for all anti-establishment candidates."
## **Gaza and Economic Frustration Dovetail**
The Democratic trifecta culminated with an acrimonious intra-party lame duck fight at the end of 2024, as pro-business Democrat House Speaker **Joe Tate** sat on popular bills, including nine that passed the legislature. Among them, legislation to lower healthcare costs for unions, expand working class tax credits, address predatory debt collectors, and fund an African-American history museum.
Democrats had lost the house in the November election, and instead of sending the bills to Whitmer for a signature before the trifecta ended, Tate handed them to incoming GOP leadership, which also refused to send them to the governor.
The state supreme court, controlled by Democrats, ruled several weeks ago that the bills had to be sent to Whitmer for signatures. Instead, Whitmer quickly vetoed them.
Labor viewed Whitmer's move as a "betrayal," a top official with one of the state's largest unions, who declined to use their name to speak freely, told Drop Site. Michigan is a labor stronghold, but 50 years of establishment policies weakened it. Too many Democrats still try to "walk the line" between corporate and labor interests, the union official said.
"When we took back the trifecta for the first time in 40 years, it was great that the party in charge shifted, but the reality is that the largest corporations in the state still were the ones who were setting the agenda at the governing table," the union official added.
Increasingly, the union has a hardline position, the official added: "You fight for workers or you do the bidding of corporations, but you cannot do both as Democrats have tried, and there's a reckoning right now because of that."
However, there is no labor effort to support "leftist" candidates, the official said. Instead, they back candidates who unequivocally choose workers over corporate interests. In Michigan, that more frequently means candidates like El-Sayed, who also received a major endorsement from the American Federation of Teachers that is part of the AFL-CIO, and even a Wayne County Sheriff's Office union. Rabhi, a union member who has joined others on the picket line, has support from the local teachers' union that has never previously endorsed in a mayoral race, he said. Local chapters of AFSCME and the UAW have also endorsed him, as have the AFT and National Nurses' Union, among others.
This translates into material support on the ground. Earlier this year, in Three Rivers--the type of small, west Michigan town where El-Sayed needs to do well to win the nomination--he joined a UAW picket line. The union won an $8 per hour raise in a 10-day strike, and, in response, the union mobilized a door knocking campaign for El-Sayed, who won over some Trump voters there.
The UAW also took a surprise step in voting to divest from Israel over its genocide, which drew [retribution](https://substack.com/redirect/dfa54225-59d9-4621-adf7-803db9627a20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the Trump administration. Meanwhile, economic discontent among Michigan's Arab-American and Muslim communities added to frustration over establishment hostility to Arab-Americans and pro-Palestinian advocates.
The establishment ignored the 100,000 "uncommitted votes" in Michigan's 2024 Democratic presidential primary, and steadfastly refused to change course on its support for Israel's genocide. Though no data on how many uncommitted voters did not vote for Kamala Harris in the general exists, she lost the state by 80,000 votes, and election data showed [a loss of about](https://substack.com/redirect/143ead61-2aae-454f-8438-a2c2526417e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 22,000 votes in the three cities with the highest Arab-American and Muslim populations alone.
It appears the establishment learned little. It launched attacks in late March against El-Sayed for campaigning with **Hasan Piker** , broadly over their criticisms of Israel. The media attacks, led by State Sen. **Mallory McMorrow** , then El-Sayed's opponent, came as Israel was invading Lebanon, and destroying cities in which many local Lebanese-Americans have roots, family members, and friends. Some [community leaders warned](https://substack.com/redirect/b7181151-0ab9-4d14-852f-2741063ff606?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Democratic establishment was ignoring their pain, and making the same mistakes as 2024.
Weeks later, Gaza and economic discontent drove upsets at a contentious April Democratic nominating convention, where leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney **Amir Makled** beat the pro-Israel, establishment candidate **Jordan Acker** for University of Michigan regent. Acker had led the U-M attack on pro-Palestinian students. And **Eli Savit** , a progressive prosecutor, defeated the [corporate, pro-Israel-backed](https://substack.com/redirect/5635fce7-d832-4f30-89fc-d4b93f5745b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Karen MacDonald** for the state attorney general.
Within months of the Piker controversy, McMorrow dropped out as she lagged in the polls, and El-Sayed broke out as the front runner.
The economic frustration is not separate from dismay over establishment support for Israel for Arab-American and Muslim voters here, and Gaza is many issues wrapped into one, said **Bilal Baydoun** , a political analyst in Dearborn.
"Supporting the genocide in Gaza is a statement on where Democratic priorities are and it's an identifier where people say 'Look they're sending billions of dollars to Israel, and I haven't heard of anything they're doing for my kids,'" Baydoun said. "People say 'I was able to afford a home in my country--I don't think my kid can do that anymore.'"
[A survey conducted in April, sponsored by Drop Site News and Zeteo,](https://substack.com/redirect/3611ae2c-8c20-437f-b1e2-4cc1ec08e725?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that 62% of Michigan Democratic primary voters agreed that they are less likely to trust a candidate would stand up for Michiganders in general if they won't stand up to AIPAC; 13% disagreed with this sentiment.
## **Can Anti-Establishment Candidates Win in Detroit and Ann Arbor?**
In Ann Arbor, where Rabhi and a slate of four other candidates are attempting to put a major dent in the corporate political machine that has ruled for 12 years, voters' concerns are a microcosm of the state and federal levels.
"People say that for 12 years the rent has gone up, the cost of living has gone up, the roads have fallen apart, and city services have not been meeting the needs of the residents," Rabhi said.
But Michigan is a diverse state and though the 15 candidates generally support the same policies, campaigning on the east side of Ann Arbor may look different than on the east of Detroit.
One recent poll shows El-Sayed behind in Detroit 66-33. Part of this may be the conservative older population. And[ tensions exist](https://substack.com/redirect/ddc781d0-ed02-4c42-8ee3-6faf2b498ff8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between [Black people and Arab-Americans ](https://substack.com/redirect/dbe13e49-87d0-4b4e-906a-9f7e4e9ce0d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in Detroit, which [in part stems from](https://substack.com/redirect/c515c62a-dff1-471c-955d-8377fbf7450d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) anger with gas station, party store, and grocery store owners in the city who are largely Chaldean and are accused of mistreating their mostly Black customers.
Some, like Eboni Taylor, a Sanders endorsee running for in a state Senate district on Detroit's largely Black east side, actively avoid the "leftist" label, and make clear they do not have an association with the DSA.
While campaigning, Taylor talks about maternal health, bringing down childcare costs, and rejecting corporate money because "these are common sense things that people want," Taylor said. "Working class families are waiting their turn to be heard and for policy to work for them, and that's what is resonating for them with my campaign."
When she navigates nursing homes or other areas where her list of progressive endorsements does not carry a lot of currency, she connects with people by talking about her history in the Baptist church, struggles raising kids, and watching her working class parents who still live in the same east side home build a better life for her.
However, Detroit City Council Member **Denzel McCampbell** , a former spokesperson for Rep. Rashida Tlaib, openly campaigned and won this cycle as a DSA member in a largely Black, low-income district on Detroit's west side, and survived his opponents attacking him for being socialist.
"On the doors, what it meant to be a socialist did not come up - what came up is 'You're not going to sell us out, right?'" McCampbell said. "That's what's connecting--'Are you going to be an authentic leader that fights for us?'"
### **Key Michigan races:**
* **Abdul El-Sayed** versus Rep. **Haley Stevens** for U.S. Senate.
* **Bernie Sanders** -endorsed former Sunrise co-founder **William Lawrence** is running against two establishment candidates, **Matt Maasdam** and **Bridget Brink** in the 7th Congressional district.
* Justice Democrats/Sanders-backed **Donovan McKinney** is running against the AIPAC-backed incumbent **Shri Thanedar** in the 3rd Congressional district.
* DSA member U.S. Rep. **Rashida Tlaib** is running for re-election against the establishment-backed Inkster Mayor **Byron Nolen** in the 12th Congressional district.
* Uncommitted co-founder and Sanders-endorsed **Abbas Alawieh** is running against state Rep. **Erin Byrnes** in Michigan state Senate district 2.
* Leftist former state Rep. **Abe Aiyash** is running against establishment pick **Justin Onwenu** in Michigan state Senate district 1.
* Sanders-endorsed **Eboni Taylor** is running against a long list of establishment-backed candidates in Michigan State Senate district 3, including Whitmer administration veteran **Korey Hall**.
* DSA and WFP-backed **Chris Gilmer-Hill** is running against incumbent state Rep. **Helena Scott** in Michigan state House district 8.
* Progressive prosecutor **Eli Savit** beat the establishment and pro-Israel-backed candidate, **Karen McDonald** , for state attorney general at the April Democratic nominating convention.
* Leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney **Amir Makled** beat the establishment, pro-Israel-backed candidate, **Jordan Acker** , for U-M board of regents at the April Democratic nominating convention.
* DSA member **Yousef Rabhi** is running for mayor of Ann Arbor with a slate of four other leftists candidates who are running for city council seats. **Chris Taylor** is the incumbent mayor.
* DSA member and former Tlaib staffer **Denzel McCampbell** won a seat on the Detroit City Council in late 2025, defeating former state Rep. **Karen Whitsett**.
* DSA State Rep. **Dylan Wegela** , WFP-backed State Rep. **Tonya Phillips** , and WFP-backed **Jason Morgan** are all defending seats in the Michigan House.

It appears the establishment learned little. It launched attacks in late March against El-Sayed for campaigning with Hasan Piker , broadly over their criticisms of Israel. The media attacks, led by State Sen. Mallory McMorrow , then El-Sayed's opponent, came as Israel was invading Lebanon, and destroying cities in which many local Lebanese-Americans have roots, family members, and friends. Some that the Democratic establishment was ignoring their pain, and making the same mistakes as 2024. Weeks later, Gaza and economic discontent drove upsets at a contentious April Democratic nominating convention, where leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney Amir Makled beat the pro-Israel, establishment candidate Jordan Acker for University of Michigan regent. Acker had led the U-M attack on pro-Palestinian students. And Eli Savit , a progressive prosecutor, defeated the Karen MacDonald for the state attorney general. Within months of the Piker controversy, McMorrow dropped out as she lagged in the polls, and El-Sayed broke out as the front runner. The economic frustration is not separate from dismay over establishment support for Israel for Arab-American and Muslim voters here, and Gaza is many issues wrapped into one, said Bilal Baydoun , a political analyst in Dearborn. "Supporting the genocide in Gaza is a statement on where Democratic priorities are and it's an identifier where people say 'Look they're sending billions of dollars to Israel, and I haven't heard of anything they're doing for my kids,'" Baydoun said. "People say 'I was able to afford a home in my country--I don't think my kid can do that anymore.'" found that 62% of Michigan Democratic primary voters agreed that they are less likely to trust a candidate would stand up for Michiganders in general if they won't stand up to AIPAC; 13% disagreed with this sentiment. Can Anti-Establishment Candidates Win in Detroit and Ann Arbor? In Ann Arbor, where Rabhi and a slate of four other candidates are attempting to put a major dent in the corporate political machine that has ruled for 12 years, voters' concerns are a microcosm of the state and federal levels. "People say that for 12 years the rent has gone up, the cost of living has gone up, the roads have fallen apart, and city services have not been meeting the needs of the residents," Rabhi said. But Michigan is a diverse state and though the 15 candidates generally support the same policies, campaigning on the east side of Ann Arbor may look different than on the east of Detroit. One recent poll shows El-Sayed behind in Detroit 66-33. Part of this may be the conservative older population. And between Detroit, which anger with gas station, party store, and grocery store owners in the city who are largely Chaldean and are accused of mistreating their mostly Black customers. Some, like Eboni Taylor, a Sanders endorsee running for in a state Senate district on Detroit's largely Black east side, actively avoid the "leftist" label, and make clear they do not have an association with the DSA. While campaigning, Taylor talks about maternal health, bringing down childcare costs, and rejecting corporate money because "these are common sense things that people want," Taylor said. "Working class families are waiting their turn to be heard and for policy to work for them, and that's what is resonating for them with my campaign." When she navigates nursing homes or other areas where her list of progressive endorsements does not carry a lot of currency, she connects with people by talking about her history in the Baptist church, struggles raising kids, and watching her working class parents who still live in the same east side home build a better life for her. However, Detroit City Council Member Denzel McCampbell , a former spokesperson for Rep. Rashida Tlaib, openly campaigned and won this cycle as a DSA member in a largely Black, low-income district on Detroit's west side, and survived his opponents attacking him for being socialist. "On the doors, what it meant to be a socialist did not come up - what came up is 'You're not going to sell us out, right?'" McCampbell said. "That's what's connecting--'Are you going to be an authentic leader that fights for us?'" Key Michigan races: Abdul El-Sayed versus Rep. Haley Stevens for U.S. Senate. Bernie Sanders -endorsed former Sunrise co-founder William Lawrence is running against two establishment candidates, Matt Maasdam and Bridget Brink in the 7th Congressional district. Justice Democrats/Sanders-backed Donovan McKinney is running against the AIPAC-backed incumbent Shri Thanedar in the 3rd Congressional district. DSA member U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib is running for re-election against the establishment-backed Inkster Mayor Byron Nolen in the 12th Congressional district. Uncommitted co-founder and Sanders-endorsed Abbas Alawieh is running against state Rep. Erin Byrnes in Michigan state Senate district 2. Leftist former state Rep. Abe Aiyash is running against establishment pick Justin Onwenu in Michigan state Senate district 1. Sanders-endorsed Eboni Taylor is running against a long list of establishment-backed candidates in Michigan State Senate district 3, including Whitmer administration veteran Korey Hall. DSA and WFP-backed Chris Gilmer-Hill is running against incumbent state Rep. Helena Scott in Michigan state House district 8. Progressive prosecutor Eli Savit beat the establishment and pro-Israel-backed candidate, Karen McDonald , for state attorney general at the April Democratic nominating convention. Leftist, pro-Palestinian attorney Amir Makled beat the establishment, pro-Israel-backed candidate, Jordan Acker , for U-M board of regents at the April Democratic nominating convention. DSA member Yousef Rabhi is running for mayor of Ann Arbor with a slate of four other leftists candidates who are running for city council seats. Chris Taylor is the incumbent mayor. DSA member and former Tlaib staffer Denzel McCampbell won a seat on the Detroit City Council in late 2025, defeating former state Rep. Karen Whitsett. DSA State Rep. Dylan Wegela , WFP-backed State Rep. Tonya Phillips , and WFP-backed Jason Morgan are all defending seats in the Michigan House. ## Amanda Bell for Congress
---
|
---
#### Volunteer activities for Amanda Bell in the week before the Primary!
By Donna Richards **Social media – share to all formats and groups.**
* Follow her FB page at Amanda Bell for Congress, and share with others.
* Place her videos on your group pages. Write comments all over the web.
* Post to tell your friends and groups that you are supporting her. Remind everyone of Aug 11 primary date. It is too late to register on-line for August, but can register and vote at the clerk’s offices before the election or at the polls on election day.

**Wear a button, and encourage strangers to ask about her. Get out there and talk to people - Role play** **Hand out cards at events or in front of the library, courthouse, grocery stores, parking lots, etc.** Walk up to someone or a group of people. I find groups to be easier.
* Are you a voter (voters?)?
* There is a primary election August 11
* I am supporting Amanda Bell for Congress, because she is the best candidate, no doubt. (Give some of her history if you want to say more.) I like her because: (Tell them why you personally like her.)
* Give them a card.
* Please learn more about her, and talk about her, and I hope you decide to vote for her on August 11. If she wins the primary.... she then goes up against Glenn Grothman in November. (You know who Glenn Grothman is!) We really have a chance to beat him!

**Attend demonstrations.** Fond du Lac Thursdays by the Mall, Mondays in Ripon at White School House (Republican first office). **Tell people where we will be election night!!** Invite them. Schmitty’s Oar House starting when the polls close at 8 PM. Plan to come, and bring others. Great food and drinks available for purchase. N7044 Winnebago Dr, Fond Du Lac, WI 54935 **Events to go to, and talk to people, and hand out cards if you are so inclined:**
* Concerts, Bars, Church, Other gatherings
* Sporting Events (Before game probably easier than after.)
* Farmers Markets - check local rules - in Fond du Lac there’s a new rule, only on public sidewalks or parks that aren’t on the market square, different municipalities will have different rules.

**Early voting has started.** Tell everyone about this. Call the clerk’s office for early voting hours. Can vote early through Friday August 7. **Wear your button, Shirt or Other Merch.**
* Donna Richards - Media & Events Team in Fond du Lac, WI

**BONUS:** **100 Contacts Challenge: ** I loved Donna’s Suggestions and one she sent me after that was that we should all call 10 of our own contacts and remind them to vote before 8/11! I thought that was a great idea and I thought I’d up the challenge. Here’s how to participate:
1. Download the tracking sheet here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1d_yYDK-bR4q1YilPGTGkvd8_AoQsNPKS/view?usp=drive_link
2. When finished email it to stephanie@stephaniekunkel.com

If you’ve already been calling, please feel free to put those contacts on your sheet. **Anyone who contacts 100 people before 8/11 to remind them to vote - and returns a checklist to me will be invited to a special pancake breakfast post primary.** Details to follow. \- Stephanie Kunkel - Campaign Manager - Wautoma, WI
---
|
---
---
|
---
#### Early voting for this primary is open!
Don’t wait till election day when you can go to your precinct clerk and vote right now. Reach out to your clerk for more information. Find details here: https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/My-Municipal-Clerk Remember this is a closed primary so you must choose a party to and only vote in primaries for that party. If you cross the ballot to vote in another primary your ballot will not be counted. Don’t forget Amanda is running on the Democratic ticket and don’t forget to vote for Amanda Bell for the 6th Congressional District Congressional seat!
---
|
---
#### Upcoming Events
Amanda will be at these events in the coming week. She’ll also be knocking on doors in the district - so please see the events page for up-to-date appearances, canvassing opportunities, and more information! Aug 4th - Amanda is headed to the Port Washington City Council Meeting. Aug 5th - A group of volunteers from the campaign are going up to help the victims of the tornados, we’re bringing chainsaws, donation items, and our services to help clear debris, and more. Aug 7th - Beaver Dam Waste Water Treatment Meeting - 10am & The Green Lake County Fair - 2pm Aug 8th - Susie the Duck Parade in Lodi Aug 9th - Kiel Parade **NEW:** Aug 10th - 12pm - 5:15pm - We’re co-hosting a Blood Drive in Oshkosh, WI - The American Red Cross has declared the second national blood crisis in its history. All blood types are needed! Come donate with us. (We’re also looking for volunteers to help us staff as many of the Red Cross volunteers are currently assisting in Menasha. Aug 10 @ **Virtual** Listening & Problem Solving Session - Tune in here: Video call link: [https://meet.google.com/imp-jwai-vkw](https://p9t2.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a70f969e5406c1382c904fe&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmeet.google.com%2Fimp-jwai-vkw&w=68e039f025c0f2594aa3b682&c=b_6a6fd5e95d69577d7601aec9&l=en-US&s=zyKFLBZYOPrLrMmHhXtIqbvYxoc%3D) Or dial: ‪(US) +1 443-914-3041‬ PIN: ‪386 857 587‬#
#### Aug 11th:
#### VOTE FOR AMANDA IN THE PRIMARY
Find your polling place and hours here: https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/find-my-polling-place Check Facebook, YouTube, and TikTok throughout the day to tune in Live and chat as we work on getting people out to the polls to Goat the Vote! For more information on any of these events or to volunteer to help email admin@amandabellforcongress.org

name: Stacy Garrity
subject: I sat down with NEPA Farmers. Here's what they told me.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Garrity for PA * 4075 Linglestown Rd PMB 119 * Harrisburg, PA 17112-1020 * USA
body:
Red tape, the death tax, and the fight to keep family farms alive.

| | | | | [|
---](http://www.garrityforpa.com)
| | | | | | Peter,
Last week, I held our campaign’s first agriculture listening session at Keith Eckel’s farm in Clarks Summit, Lackawanna County. I sat with farmers, legislators, and local leaders to talk about the issues facing the Ag community.
I heard that farming in Pennsylvania gets harder every day. And too often, it’s state government making it harder.
---
|
---
| | Here’s what I heard:
**Jim Barbour** , a third-generation dairy and beef farmer from Susquehanna County, said his farm is looking for state programs to help. His experience? “Everybody says, ‘Oh, there’s grant money everywhere until you go finding it, and then you can’t find it.’” He said the different state offices don’t communicate with each other, and that’s exactly why he supports my plan for a one-stop FARM office.
**Keith Eckel** , former President of the Pennsylvania Farm Bureau and a Lackawanna County farmer, talked about the inheritance tax. Four of his aunts were farmers, and each time one of them passed away, the family had to pay a 15% inheritance tax on the farm. He called it a critical issue that needs to be addressed if we’re serious about preserving agriculture in Pennsylvania.
---
| | | | |
---
| | Senator Lisa Baker, who has co-sponsored bills to eliminate the inheritance tax, said it plainly: when someone loses a family member and then has to make a decision about selling their property to just pay the tax, that is not fair.
We also discussed permitting reform. State Representative Jon Fritz, who has authored legislation to deem permits approved after 45 days, said what every farmer in the room was thinking: **Pennsylvania should be rolling out the red carpet for agriculture, not busting out the red tape.**
This is what leadership looks like.
You show up. You listen. You learn what’s actually happening on our farms.
At the end of the roundtable, I told the group what I believe: cut red tape, get rid of the overregulation, get rid of the death tax, expand markets for Pennsylvania-grown and raised products, and preserve our precious farmland and help grow the next generation of Pennsylvania farmers.
Food security is national security. And Pennsylvania’s farmers are on the front lines.
---

body:
(Derek, my friend Tim Kaine asked me to reach out with some thoughts before Virginia’s Primary tomorrow. I hope you’ll take a few minutes to read it – but if you’re short on time, and you’re already committed to helping Virginia Democrats win BIG this November, you can split a donation at this link: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner] )
Derek –
I’ve been in public service long enough to recognize that every two years, folks claim the November elections are the most important ever. I know it can be hard to believe.
But I’m here to tell you that this year, I mean it.
Why? Because in all my years serving Virginians – as your Governor and now as your Senator – I’ve never seen anything like this second Trump administration.
* The president’s backwards and dangerous agenda is skyrocketing your costs at the grocery store and the gas pump due to his war of choice in Iran and reckless tariffs.

* His erratic leadership has damaged America’s standing on the world stage, alienating our allies and making us all less safe.

* His cruel policies have gutted health care access for millions of Americans, all to pay for tax breaks for those at the very top.

* And he’s peddling unhinged conspiracy theories about our elections – claiming the 2020 election he lost was rigged, sending the federal government to seize voter rolls in states like Georgia, and he seems to be laying the groundwork to federalize elections.
Never in my lifetime did I think we would see this kind of crap – and far too many of my Republican colleagues refuse to stand up and hold this administration accountable.
It’s clear to me that the only way to finally put some checks and balances on this administration is to flip the balance of power in Congress. That means organizing everywhere, competing for every last vote, and electing Democrats up and down the ballot who will fight for working families and defend our democracy.
And Derek, Virginia has a critical role to play. Not only do we have a Senate seat to defend, but across our Commonwealth, there are battleground House seats that will determine control of Congress.
Tomorrow, voters will decide the party nominees in must-win races across Virginia. Once the stage is set, we will officially enter the general election – and the final, all-out sprint until Election Day.
I’m committed to giving my all – not just in my own race, but in races up and down the ballot to elect Virginia Democrats and flip control of Congress.
But in order to hit the ground running after the primary, we need to raise the resources we need to reach as many voters as possible and turn them out to vote.
That’s why my campaign has set a Primary Day goal of raising $25,000 before the polls close on Tuesday. The resources we amass now help run TV and digital ads, recruit volunteers, and knock on doors in the communities that will decide these races.
The clock is ticking. Can you split a donation today between my campaign and Tim Kaine's Common Ground PAC to help me hit this critical goal and start the general election in a strong position so we can win big in the fall? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?amount=25]

Peter,
**Waking up every day to watch this administration dismantle our democracy piece by piece is absolutely infuriating.**
And honestly, we don’t have the luxury of playing nice and waiting around for our leaders to wake the hell up. Not when the fights we’re up against are this dire.
Trump is waging an illegal war in Iran that's already cost American taxpayers _$36 billion_. Gas is getting higher by the minute, grocery bills keep climbing, and millions of people can’t afford to go to the doctor. Working families are being left to survive a corrupt political system that continues to put the wealthy and powerful first.
This is the moment to go all in. We have to fight back on every front, with every tool at our disposal, and do more than just react. **We have to build.**
**[Rush a $5 donation right now to help Leaders We Deserve do just that.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260803_1_resendinf.NaFvNd&refcode=em20260803-3813&amount=5&t=2&akid=3813%2E587540%2E4HRRkl)**
**That means defeating Republicans** in red-to-blue races in state legislatures and in Congress to ensure there’s a real check on Trump’s authoritarian agenda.
**It means primarying asleep-at-the-wheel Democrats** because if they’re not fighting tooth and nail to defeat the Trump agenda and deliver real change for the people, they’re in the way. After losing twice to Trump, it could not be more clear that the leaders who got us into this mess are not the ones who will get us out of it.
**It means offering voters a vision worth believing in.** Momentum is on our side, but with 92 days left until November, the window to make it count is _right now._
We need to throw every ounce of support behind the leaders who feel the urgency of this moment in their bones and a fire in their belly to transform the broken system they grew up in.
**That’s what Leaders We Deserve was built for.** To find fearless candidates who refuse to sit on the sidelines while their communities get left behind, put real resources behind their campaigns, and prove the establishment doesn’t get to decide what the face of power looks like anymore.
And right now, we need you in this fight with us.

If I ran into you at the gas pump, I wouldn't ask you for a campaign contribution.
I'd probably ask how you're doing, how your family's doing, or whether there's anything I should know that's making life harder in your community.
The truth is, I don't enjoy sending emails like these. I'd much rather be out in Southwest Washington talking with people, visiting small businesses, touring a day care, or rolling up my sleeves to solve problems.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
That's the job.
And together, we've gotten a lot done.
We've worked across party lines to expand child care in rural communities, cut unnecessary red tape, and focused on the practical, everyday issues that too often get ignored in Washington.
None of those ideas came from a political consultant—they came from listening to people right here at home.
But here's the reality: national MAGA Republicans have made this one of their top targets because they want to take this seat away from the people of Washington's Third District.
I hate asking.
But I hate the idea of handing this seat over to people who are more interested in partisan fights than practical solutions even more.

body:
My visit to Austin17House

| |
---
| | Dear David, A couple of weeks ago, I had the privilege of visiting one of the most remarkable and uplifting places I have ever been. In January 2017, Mark Anderson founded Austin17House as a safe haven for youth who weren’t being served by traditional educational and community institutions. He was inspired to found the community center after witnessing the outpouring of love and support that came after he lost his son, Austin, at the age of 17 in a drug-related car accident. **Austin17House was founded in the spirit of love, and it shows.** As I toured the facility with Mark, we met incredible staff and volunteers like Justin, who said it was his mission to be the adult to the kids at Austin17House that he needed when he was a young person struggling to find his way in life. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/SX6GG9ROa4NOdWB57kBH4w~~/AAUS1hA~/GxdBplyGpzlJAj73-js-UqhYOePo5-6CuLfxE8s8pQSywXwVJ0MKlION-fYvI4G26y6-ZVVPQMFwcz7_tMwMntSunO5w1Xu0tgHPKAqtNGRItXWb7okDYqG3uVZjT4dPl77wONz0Z6jTIWw-OxLdlP11WoBpY6g81IynpV3O7nvPzTyOaALmtamqUtK0ppQbqKi_tEB-Aj16RYsOX-aj_NMn3oeXKs55A5NFbxv1tf2x5ljQs43J9vsoC_vXx0mwUDW-QPYX00_Z8K1NbvmeUA~~)
_Mark and Justin give me hope that strong communities can heal a broken world._ In addition to love, I was struck by the sense of purpose that infused everything that was happening at Austin17House. From the kitchen to the woodshop to the art room, adults and children worked side-by-side in a spirit of joy, healing, and hope. Mark’s openness and obvious passion are suffused with relentless hope and a faith in what communities can accomplish when they work together. [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/SX6GG9ROa4NOdWB57kBH4w~~/AAUS1hA~/GxdBplyGpzlJAj73-js-UqhYOePo5-6CuLfxE8s8pQSywXwVJ0MKlION-fYvI4G26y6-ZVVPQMFwcz7_tMwMntSunO5w1Xu0tgHPKAqtNGRItXWb7okDYqG3uVZjT4dPl77wONz0Z6jTIWw-OxLdlP11WoBpY6g81IynpV3O7nvPzTyOaALmtamqUtK0ppQbqKi_tEB-Aj16RYsOX-aj_NMn3oeXKs55A5NFbxv1tf2x5ljQs43J9vsoC_vXx0mwUDW-QPYX00_Z8K1NbvmeUA~~) Those are the principles I’m using to guide my campaign, David: hope, faith, and a relentless belief that we can achieve big things when we come together with a shared purpose. I’m grateful that you’ve joined me on this journey to bring a new kind of politics to Washington, and I can’t wait to see what we continue to accomplish together. Hi there,
The Kim regime spends enormous resources on one thing above everything else:
Controlling the story.
They control what their 26 million citizens see, hear, eat, and believe. They control how their country is presented to the outside world—hosting staged delegations, producing propaganda films, and silencing anyone who speaks the truth.
**What they cannot control is what happens when someone escapes. And we need your help getting the story of a North Korean survivor to the world.**
[Help get the truth to the world](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=2bf06f986f9b4ea5b41864c993e5ae18&_e=S6uTFML_Pg1nPR8gLe4jHWSZe1-7F5bhVB8EiT-TfxjDaQDUefUsy97wyRv3UdnChml1siJ7KaJ6q8vsK_7n95bIWNAGLk-VXKVNONaKqSuViGXAWjCzud9tzR3b0fte1WqHN9SzHh4r_hQLU_s6kLUcx3_b9PmmXH8gwyt6jTs7qAQ7Ef4AsNeIPd1YnGac_kKeKez5kJrMHVSM5ZBMNuwcCaHE2rlA6sQ0cZbf9wQZknc_dOfR7iu9QBU0HNbsgmMa7rYUlPmDUS3rhFZ_vIclswVUvei-H2cRmq9rpA4yD0NRcAUP-pra4sAY19PTPVyTZwwQzKhFIwRyvEa3KgHjSAZqgaxHSE9Wzje_J64gL9LZHGrm7tcDG-VY2UPMLdGr7tcpsJoMaamndKpYS2vOZ008vFhG2htiTHcxuSPwCTUqP50gorym5wSbL89ICwVggLbZjUoMJDvsyo-efuX06UUmCl5HnOVQFRH1s06uZnBida2AQ84xellpeFJFnUsE9BZtD0MFDQQmNhugI4g7c7WmAV4qPqazXj6yBpJHViFZA4n_4rssMqlMoRDMnc88G-aYX0NJmvaEs4q-xboZ5V5GuGvmrNusVvdmufDkyRNeAL9BBrRuv_X8qzrBDlq-C5_RDI6I-O7fXfoVptipWPnlLtebnHJR8C5VeoE%3D)
Yeonmi Park escaped at 13. She survived slavery in China. She crossed the Gobi Desert at night, guided by stars, and finally reached freedom in South Korea at 15. And when she got there, she refused to be silent.
**Her talks about life inside North Korea have been viewed nearly 350 million times. The regime cannot stop her voice.**
That’s why the Moving Picture Institute is producing In Order to Live: The Yeonmi Park Story—a major narrative feature made with the same production quality that has put MPI Original films on Netflix, Apple TV, Amazon Prime, and Hulu, reaching hundreds of millions of viewers worldwide.
**Will you give $25 right now to help put this story in front of millions?**
[Give $25](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=2bf06f986f9b4ea5b41864c993e5ae18&_e=S6uTFML_Pg1nPR8gLe4jHWSZe1-7F5bhVB8EiT-TfxjDaQDUefUsy97wyRv3UdnChml1siJ7KaJ6q8vsK_7n95bIWNAGLk-VXKVNONaKqSuViGXAWjCzud9tzR3b0fte1WqHN9SzHh4r_hQLU_s6kLUcx3_b9PmmXH8gwyt6jTs7qAQ7Ef4AsNeIPd1YnGac_kKeKez5kJrMHVSM5ZBMNma0C-UzgZ4wJwLYopszksWy5TYGa3vuf8X_kPs8RdqMrZSckAudnG_2PAhCPxBSlEKPReqZlq_iqOqOeKbneDlnBQUGru_vLN8EsLj1ZZr0_QNIA-WFbA7UQ1Gein9U-6uE6Xu6Wn55MCs-LapPROZ9QdQAcMjD0Ixruzcfj3XQu6mi97JUv_91OsfoVCUFXY0NRCEli2g7-AQ2_1DHf1ClpT6S0ADmqzsLrVRVliuNLBoV6_Ypkd-Feabc0TAxQx08qykVwLob90na8_--Gdpai2msIPsMTZ8Z9qZxEMyvgVCrA4M9Bd4aPT38gUeXVo9_xuGj7wk4XY-5sB0MCCC41z_z50a2hdiGIa1mhIiOjaQZvQmLAR-On7yRNYl6r5ai38ft8LqiVi2YfpOg7LYfkg8pm0dK25q1UTqLW1oLsl3KbSoGDOpxmNz5EfZ719aBrzKrQ2wNoFwBmmsgv4N3qshvN8UTXp3awMcHcIMK) [Give another amount](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=2bf06f986f9b4ea5b41864c993e5ae18&_e=S6uTFML_Pg1nPR8gLe4jHWSZe1-7F5bhVB8EiT-TfxjDaQDUefUsy97wyRv3UdnChml1siJ7KaJ6q8vsK_7n95bIWNAGLk-VXKVNONaKqSuViGXAWjCzud9tzR3b0fte1WqHN9SzHh4r_hQLU_s6kLUcx3_b9PmmXH8gwyt6jTs7qAQ7Ef4AsNeIPd1YnGac_kKeKez5kJrMHVSM5ZBMNuwcCaHE2rlA6sQ0cZbf9wSTQakPcakA_QafxHXsaMzJhgvbpfTdflCwNUATo0rk8xmPahzCEHChQ4ulN3aoQoe9jPHtGrioAEVzY7iLijYuZpgGz8tASlUJm_tJHp1-sO0rScgj_dpyetdwRqMDNszMbD09nbLWU8eWW8-TyAapow3whVwtISBVjjJPaKHlFLO7OtfwezOwy34AZopdfIJG7QQ21fwBJ5iAtLGHiS15GgHgOqOhXK0cgUTCQTvV3FTOZwxVnnfVZdRRZbQpUVY_6W-kYghMvIFPtYC3SYVNzYwh6nXGsWrmJKiVxRTvh8ljFUc7O30G752v6GIsy063Fnbc-KDtZl68NYWT7OLRpfwELm9E6ltwsJrh51FuS4XuukPcvQnM_u6pwgQMMh2BkxUw5t8R9JOaySGcCq6yf54BBW8a8k--q7boSG4jEVE13AalJKM1FhLVNAOMrD4%3D)
Great films don’t just inform people. They move them.
There is a difference between knowing that North Korea is a brutal totalitarian state and watching a real woman’s escape: her terror, her survival, and her first moment of freedom.
That is what In Order to Live will do.

clean_body: Hi there, The Kim regime spends enormous resources on one thing above everything else: Controlling the story. They control what their 26 million citizens see, hear, eat, and believe. They control how their country is presented to the outside world—hosting staged delegations, producing propaganda films, and silencing anyone who speaks the truth. What they cannot control is what happens when someone escapes. And we need your help getting the story of a North Korean survivor to the world. Yeonmi Park escaped at 13. She survived slavery in China. She crossed the Gobi Desert at night, guided by stars, and finally reached freedom in South Korea at 15. And when she got there, she refused to be silent. Her talks about life inside North Korea have been viewed nearly 350 million times. The regime cannot stop her voice. That’s why the Moving Picture Institute is producing In Order to Live: The Yeonmi Park Story—a major narrative feature made with the same production quality that has put MPI Original films on Netflix, Apple TV, Amazon Prime, and Hulu, reaching hundreds of millions of viewers worldwide. Will you give $25 right now to help put this story in front of millions? Great films don’t just inform people. They move them. There is a difference between knowing that North Korea is a brutal totalitarian state and watching a real woman’s escape: her terror, her survival, and her first moment of freedom. That is what In Order to Live will do. We tell stories for Americans like you—people who believe that truth matters and that film is one of the most powerful ways to spread it. For freedom, Joseph Corey Vice President of Philanthropic Investments The Moving Picture Institute P.S. — Yeonmi Park is serving as executive producer on this film. body:
It's hard to believe we're already in August!

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
### It’s hard to believe we’re already in August. With Election Day drawing closer, our campaign is entering one of the most important stretches of the race. In the weeks ahead, we’ll be knocking on doors, continuing to meet voters in communities across the district, and building the coalition we need to win in November. Before we dive into everything that’s ahead, I wanted to take a moment to look back at July—a month filled with incredible momentum, meaningful conversations, and milestones that brought us one step closer to our goal. None of it would have been possible without your support, and I’m so grateful to have you on this journey with me.
---
| |
### Best, Eileen.

| |
July might have been the campaign’s busiest month yet! It was packed full of events, and I enjoyed every moment of connection with the people of this district.

I visited **six counties** this month, and was able to attend a variety of different events across the district. Some of the highlights were attending the Bobstock Music Festival in Morgan County, taking my kids and grandkids to the Brush rodeo, and getting to have meaningful conversations with so many different people at my booth at Wray Daze!
It was so much fun getting to meet hundreds of people at the **five meet and greets** we held across the district in July. I was able to hear from Democrats, Republicans, and Independents alike about the challenges being faced by the people of this district, and got to tell folks about my plans to lower costs and fight corruption once I get to Congress.
There’s nothing like a summer parade, and I had so much fun marching in **four parades** this month. We started out with the Fourth of July parade in Highlands Ranch, where my grandkids and I had a blast handing out candy. I got to meet lots of great folks at the Eaton Days parade, and really enjoyed seeing all the cow-themed trucks at the Who Let the Herd Out parade in Akron. We closed out the month at the Douglas County Fair Parade in Castle Rock, where I was inspired by the number of supporters in the crowd!
I’ve been making my way across the district meeting with each hospital, and was able to visit **three hospitals** in July. It’s been a priority for me to hear directly from health care workers about the challenges they’re facing and their thoughts on how I can help support their work when I get to Congress. I heard from Wray Hospital about the difficulties of being one of the few rural hospitals on the Eastern plains that is equipped to deliver babies, and from East Morgan County Hospital about our flawed payer system. It was also very special to visit the Children’s One Hangar that services the rural hospitals of CD4.

body:
As the sun sets on Maine tonight...

| As the sun sets over the Pine Tree State tonight, it’s time for a Maine bedtime story 🌚.It’s a tale of two very different paths for Maine - and two very different leaders.On one side, you have Susan Collins: a strong, steady warrior who has dedicated her life to serving Maine. We hope to have you on our team, but if you want to opt out from future emails, you can . Heads up, Peter — Eight days from today, Vermonters will head to the polls and cast their vote in the gubernatorial primary election (for Aly, we hope!). Before then, we have LOTS of work to do — and we need your help to make the most of these last eight days! We're putting up lawn signs. We're knocking doors. We're talking to as many undecided voters as possible, sharing Aly’s plans and positive vision for what Vermont’s future can look like. But with eight days left, we're running out of time to grow our momentum. = | = = We know the majority of Vermont Democratic primary voters are still undecided — as much as 52%! That means this race is very much still Aly’s to win, but ONLY if we can get her message in front of every voter who hasn't made up their mind yet. That’s why we’re directing every dollar we raise toward doing exactly that: more signs in more yards, more conversations, more Vermonters hearing about a candidate who has actually delivered tangible results for our brave little state and is ready to do it again. Now, we’re officially in the home stretch. With eight days left in the primary, it’s time to go all-out. Hi team,
I joined some great folks doing cleanup off of Snake Road this weekend.
There was so much trash. If I were doing it by myself, it would've been demoralizing. But our community came together to clean up our roads and the beautiful woods around them.
**We need to do the same thing to our politics.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/638adb10-3ed9-4118-a42a-3ba70cd6709d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Dan Meuser has doubled his net worth in office and has never held a real town hall. Politicians like him are a big part of why so many Americans don't trust Congress.
I'm running to fix that. I'll fight to ban congressional stock trading, implement term limits, and overturn Citizens United and stop the unlimited dark money from ruining our politics.
**But I can 't do this alone. Just like Snake Road, it's going to take all of us coming together to clean up Washington.**

There was so much trash. If I were doing it by myself, it would've been demoralizing. But our community came together to clean up our roads and the beautiful woods around them. We need to do the same thing to our politics. | | ---|---|--- Dan Meuser has doubled his net worth in office and has never held a real town hall. Politicians like him are a big part of why so many Americans don't trust Congress. I'm running to fix that. I'll fight to ban congressional stock trading, implement term limits, and overturn Citizens United and stop the unlimited dark money from ruining our politics. But I can 't do this alone. Just like Snake Road, it's going to take all of us coming together to clean up Washington. Thank you for being a part of this. - Rachel Wallace Thanks for reading! subject: 🚨 August Newsletter | Important Campaign News
body:
We are only 92 days out until Election Day! With your help, we have been hard at work knocking on doors, calling voters, and sharing the importance of

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/derektranforcongress/2026-august-newsletter?e=fa48019594)
---
| | | | |
---
| | Dear Supporter,
We are only 92 days out until Election Day! With your help, we have been hard at work knocking on doors, calling voters, and sharing the importance of keeping this seat blue to hold Donald Trump accountable in November.
Since day one, our grassroots campaign has made it clear that we will not allow out-of-touch Republicans to disenfranchise our community’s voice. That’s why I’m proud to share that we raised over $1.12 million in Q2, **with an average grassroots donation of $51.49.**
These donations come from **public school teachers, first responders, and veterans across Orange and Los Angeles Counties who believe in a future where the American Dream is a reality for all.**
As we kick off the month of August, I would be honored if you [organized with us](https://www.derektranforcongress.com/getinvolved), [chipped in a few dollars](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/derek-tran-for-congress-1?refcode=newsletter), or [shared our message on social media](https://www.derektranforcongress.com/toolkit).
---
|
---
| | **CALLING VOLUNTEERS FOR OUR DIGITAL MOBILIZATION TEAM**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | Are you savvy on social media and eager to support Team Tran? We are seeking volunteers to join our **digital mobilization team**. Please submit your interest [**HERE**](https://forms.gle/QYfutamkHK279AQK9).
---
| |
---
| | **CANVASSING OPPORTUNITIES**
---
| | Starting this month, Team Tran will be **canvassing twice per week** to connect with voters on the issues. Sign up to ensure their voices are heard:
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **ARTESIA** Saturday, Aug 19 a.m. - 1 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/982564/)
**GARDEN GROVE** Sunday, Aug 23 p.m. - 7 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/990079/)
**STANTON** Saturday, Aug 89 a.m. - 1 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/989997/)
---
| | | **NORWALK** Sunday, Aug 91 p.m. - 5 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/998061/)
**FOUNTAIN VALLEY** Saturday, Aug 159 a.m. - 1 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/983563/)
**BUENA PARK** Sunday, Aug 1610 a.m. - 2 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/1002741/)
---
| | | **GARDEN GROVE** Saturday, Aug 229 a.m. - 1 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/982665/)
**WESTMINSTER** Sunday, Aug 231 p.m. - 5 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/1002751/)
**CYPRESS** Saturday, Aug 299 a.m. - 1 p.m. PSTRegister: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/derektranforcongress/event/923057/)
---
| | **SOCIAL MEDIA TOOLKIT**
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | We’re excited to share our official **campaign social media toolkit**!
Download graphics shareable for social media at our [**website**](http://derektranforcongress.com/toolkit) to help spread our message and keep CA-45 blue this November.
Follow Team Tran on [**Instagram**](https://instagram.com/derektranca) , [**Facebook**](https://facebook.com/derektranforcongress) , [**X**](https://twitter.com/DerekTranCA45) , and [**TikTok**](https://www.tiktok.com/@derektranca45). Tag us on social media using **#DerekTranForCongress**.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **REQUEST A YARD SIGN TODAY** Excited about a Democratic House majority this November? Share your pride with a **free** **Derek Tran for Congress yard sign**. Request a yard sign: [**HERE**](https://www.derektranforcongress.com/getinvolved)
---
| | | **JOIN A VIRTUAL PHONE BANK** Join the **California Democratic Party** every Wednesday, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. PST, to call voters across the district, hear what issues matter most to them, and share our platform for working families. Register: [**HERE**](https://www.mobilize.us/cadems/event/887949/)
---
|
---
| | **ENDORSEMENTS**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | “Southern California families deserve a fighter in Congress who is focused on lowering costs, protecting our democracy, and creating a more equal and just world. In his first term, Rep. Tran has delivered for working families, standing up to Donald Trump’s extreme, billionaire-first agenda. We are proud to support Rep. Tran’s reelection to continue advocating for families across Southern California,” **said Katie Bethell, Executive Director of MoveOn.**
---
| |
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | “A father of young children and member of the Congressional Dads Caucus, Rep. Tran knows from personal experience how our country’s care and affordability crises are harming young families, as well as businesses and our economy. He is a powerful champion for policies that will put quality, affordable child care within reach for all children and families, pressing every day for the solutions we need,” **said Kristin Rowe-Finkbeiner, Executive Director and CEO of MomsRising.**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | “As an Army Veteran and a father of three kids, I have advocated for gun violence prevention measures to keep our communities safe. These common-sense strategies, including universal background checks and secure firearm storage, have strong bipartisan support among voters and in Congress. I’m proud to be in this fight with Moms Demand Action, and I’m committed to making sure we all feel safe in our communities,”**said Congressman Tran.**
---
| |
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | “As a champion of students, teachers, and families, Derek has fought hard against harmful attempts to dismantle our public education. He understands the importance of preparing every student for success in a diverse and evolving world. Derek shares our values and commitment to public education,” **said CTA President David B. Goldberg.**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | “Derek has been a strong champion for Southern California’s coasts and the environment. In Congress, Derek has fought the impacts of climate change and has protected access to public lands for future generations. We need people like Derek in Congress to continue supporting Southern California communities. The NRDC Action Fund is proud to support Derek Tran for Congress,” **said Jed Ober, Managing Director of NRDC Action Fund.**
---
| |
---
|
---
| | **FOUNTAIN VALLEY MEET AND GREET**
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | I was in **Fountain Valley** meeting with local leaders and neighbors who shared the importance of federal resources supporting the community.
**Just last month, I secured $2 million to strengthen the fire department’s emergency response operations.**
---
| | **LOS CERRITOS DEMOCRATIC CLUB**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | I was grateful to earn the endorsement of the **Los Cerritos Democratic Club** during their July meeting.
**Because of our strong grassroots momentum, we’re sending a loud message to national Republicans that CA-45 can’t be bought this November.**
---
| |
---
| | **LAKEWOOD MEET AND GREET**
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | It was great to join **Lakewood** residents and Mayor Cassandra Chase for a meet and greet.
**We talked about lowering costs for working families and how I’ve brought taxpayer dollars back into Lakewood.**
---
| | **REP. JOHN LEWIS CANDLELIGHT VIGIL**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | Our **Democracy Summer Fellows** joined Indivisible CA-45 to celebrate and honor the life of late Congressman John Lewis.
**It’s up to us to defend his legacy and mission to create a more equal and just country for all.**
---
| |
---
| | **FINAL 100 DAYS INTERNSHIP PROGRAM**
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | Team Tran welcomed over **30 interns and fellows** part of our organizing team.
**If you would like to support these hardworking high school and college students**, please email Ethan Sternberg at [**ethan@derektranforcongress.com**](mailto:ethan@derektranforcongress.com?subject=I%20would%20like%20to%20support%20interns%20with%20Team%20Tran&body=Hi%20Ethan%2C%0AI%20would%20love%20to%20support%20interns%20with%20Team%20Tran.%20How%20can%20I%20help%3F).
---
| | **LEGISLATIVE WINS**
---
| | _**Congressman Derek Tran Introduces Bill to Fight Back Against Abusive ICE Detention Centers**_
---
| | To fight back against the abusive and harmful tactics used at U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention centers, frontline candidate and Democratic nominee Derek Tran, who represents the most competitive House seat in Southern California, introduced legislation to hold privately-owned detention centers accountable.The _Private Detention Corporate Accountability Act of 2026_ would allow families of deceased detainees to seek damages starting at $5 million as the result of a wrongful death in the detention center’s care. Read more: [**HERE**](https://www.derektranforcongress.com/news/congressman-derek-tran-introduces-bill-to-fight-back-against-abusive-ice-detention-centers)
---
| | _**Congressman Derek Tran Secures $250,000 to Strengthen Public Safety Infrastructure in Fullerton**_
---
| | Today, frontline candidate and Democratic nominee Derek Tran, who represents the most competitive House seat in Southern California, secured $250,000 for the City of Fullerton to strengthen its public safety infrastructure.
This funding will improve street infrastructure, fix damaged sidewalks, build accessible curb ramps, and renew existing roadway drainage. Congressman Tran is committed to bringing back federal investments to Southern California to improve public safety and the lives of working families. Read more: [**HERE**](https://www.derektranforcongress.com/news/congressman-derek-tran-secures-250000-to-strengthen-public-safety-infrastructure-in-fullerton)
---
|

---

| | Join our movement today to continue building a better future for those in California’s 45th Congressional District.
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%._ _It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._
_Use of Derek Tran's military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the Dept. of Defense or U.S. Army._

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. Hello Peter, and happy eight-days-until-the-primary! Brewery stops, beach days, creemee meet-ups, honk and waves, concerts...the next 8 days are going to be a blast! **_But my big ask_ : join a Get Out the Vote Phonebank.** The #1 thing that helps decide elections in a primary? Voter contact - hands down. Calls are easy, the conversations have been lovely (truthfully!) and you don't need prior experience. Primary turnout is historically low - talking to Vermonters gets them to the polls! And now, you can call with us **_in person_** at the Burlington campaign HQ! **VOLUNTEER NEEDS:**
* GOTV PHONE BANK VOLUNTEERS. _We've got a physical campaign office on Church Street! _
* Polling place signage! If you have a lawn sign, please set it up at your polling place for the day (following the rules, of course) and bring it home with you in the evening. Some locations let you set them up the night before, some the day of at 7AM. Check with your town clerk!
* Come to an event with us. There's a lot of joy to be had!

body:
Taking back Texas this year is in our sights.

| | |
---
Friend —
I need you to sit with this number for a second: **one point.**
That's it. That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12149?refcode=jtk1150-bu-nd&t=1&akid=11483%2E400544%2EwgiDE2)
In nearly twelve years as governor, through three elections, Greg Abbott has never faced a poll this close. _Not once._ His campaign has already spent over $54 million this cycle just to hang on to power. This poll says people aren’t buying what he’s selling anymore.
Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Nearly 4 in 10 Texans say inflation is the top issue on their minds — **and after 12 years of Greg Abbott, they're done waiting around for things to get better.**
I'm not surprised. I've been hearing it at every stop — from Brownsville to Austin to Amarillo. Families are tired of watching their grocery bills and insurance premiums climb while Abbott hands billions to his donors.
**This 1-point poll shows that a new chapter for Texas is finally in reach.** But it’s not guaranteed. Turnout will decide this election. And Abbott's team knows it — they're going to spend the next **92** days doing everything they can to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up to the polls to vote. They will do anything to keep Texans from turning the page on his failed administration.
I can't outspend Greg Abbott, and I don’t need to. Our campaign can out-organize him, but that takes people like you stepping up right now to raise the resources we need to win this race.

That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News. Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Medicaid expansion increased demand for healthcare services that hospitals are required to sell at a loss. Predictably, hospitals began losing so much money they were forced to close. Now "Medicare for All" is the new empty slogan.
Maine's rural hospitals, the ones that are still open, are in crisis. Like arsonists playing firemen, Democratic candidates Hannah Pingree and Troy Jackson are claiming to have some socialist solution to fix healthcare in Maine while casting blame on Republican President Donald Trump and Senator Susan Collins (R).
But any honest diagnosis of what ails Maine's medical industry must begin with the acknowledgement that Maine Democrats have exercised unilateral control over healthcare policy since Gov. Janet Mills (D) entered office. During that time, Hannah Pingree was her top policy advisor and Troy Jackson was the most powerful Democratic lawmaker in the state. Every healthcare policy in the state happened with their approval, including the expansion of a bloated, fraud-ridden welfare program that chronically underpays Maine's hospitals, i.e. Medicaid, known in Maine as MaineCare.
