In 2010, fewer than 300,000 Maine residents were on the welfare program. Gov. Paul LePage's reforms -- like requiring welfare seekers to work -- reduced that to fewer than 240,000 by 2018. By the end of his two terms, LePage was able to get the number of medical welfare recipients to less than 17.3 percent of the population. At the same time, LePage paid down a mammoth Baldacci-era hospital debt, an act of fiscal prudence that indisputably helped the hospitals stay operational. During that time, Maine saw nothing like the current epidemic of hospital closures.
Then came Medicaid expansion.
In the election of Gov. Mills, the DSA-controlled Democratic Party got everything they wanted, a proverbial blank check to pass whatever healthcare fixes Big Bad LePage had vetoed. As Mills' first act in office (one day after celebrating her inauguration with the Chinese Consul General of NYC Huang Ping), Mills brought to fruition the decade-long leftist scheme -- hatched under President Barack Obama's Affordable Care Act (aka ObamaCare) -- and added almost 100,000 young adults to the welfare rolls. These were able-bodied childless Maine residents with no excuse not to work. In addition, Democrats inexplicably redefined children to include 19- and 20-year-olds for the purpose of keeping them on welfare. They would later add a broad class of non-citizens, including those 19- and 20-year-old noncitizen "children" -- a population that the non-insane among us would call military-aged illegal aliens and asylum fraudsters.
In short, Mills gave the far left all the socialized medicine and multicultural welfare they'd been yammering about for a decade. Don't want to work? Just arrived in the U.S.? Ready to drop an anchor baby? No problem, you've got free health care, an EBT card, and likely some free housing, too, courtesy of the class of Mainers with callouses on their hands and small businesses to run. That's the Maine Democrats' health care policy in a nutshell: take from productive people to reward non-productive people and non-citizens.
In their view, there could be no possible downside or negative consequences to spreading the wealth around by growing the MaineCare program. The massive growth of the welfare state would not only bring about economic equality and stronger public health, the advocates said, but it would also be an economic panacea. Expanding MaineCare, they claimed, would save Maine's healthcare system, make Mainers healthier, and even invigorate our economy with a flood of federal matching dollars.
Janet Mills [said](https://substack.com/redirect/dbb66edf-b206-43b0-a304-44bec8593421?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) MaineCare expansion would "improve the health of Mainers. It will inject millions of dollars into our economy. It will create jobs, lower health care costs for Maine people and keep our rural hospitals open." (emphasis added) Calling MaineCare expansion a "huge win," Senate President Troy Jackson [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ad3f44dd-0953-4c7c-8b72-edcadbce6c04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) growing the welfare rolls would "strengthen our rural hospitals, help combat the opioid epidemic, stabilize the cost of health care for insured Mainers and make sure eligible folks can finally get health insurance." (emphasis added)
How's that working out? Spoiler alert: The rural hospitals are closing, the opioid epidemic is surging, health insurance costs for working Mainers are soaring, and the only economic stimulus has been for the guys selling Mercedes G-Wagons to Central African asylum fraudsters. Virtually every promise Democrats made about Medicaid expansion resulted in the opposite happening.
The only thing that actually came true was that more than one hundred thousand people were added to the welfare rolls. By 2023, about 370,000 Mainers were enrolled in MaineCare -- roughly 28 percent of the state's population. In Oct. 2023, DHHS bragged that the expansion population alone included 106,587 people, of whom 94,407 were adults without children. DHHS [deleted](https://substack.com/redirect/90c60ecc-362f-45c8-b715-592c837e892c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that [webpage](https://substack.com/redirect/90c60ecc-362f-45c8-b715-592c837e892c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for some odd reason around Feb. 2026, but the [archive](https://substack.com/redirect/cedbca94-674c-4cd9-8731-7b827c96bcf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) remains available for viewing. DHHS refuses to say how many noncitizens have been added to the Medicaid rolls, but it's safe to say that number is somewhere between 25,000 and 50,000, based on estimates from the migrant NGOs.
So why did Democrats' vaunted Medicaid expansion backfire spectacularly and corrode the healthcare economy in Maine?
The short answer: Math.
The longer answer is that Medicaid radically underpays for all services. In fact, Maine's largest hospitals lose hundreds of millions of dollars every year to provide care to the Medicaid population. MaineHealth's [2023 Form 990](https://substack.com/redirect/511e6ddf-9734-45fc-a541-9eab3b2fe080?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) lays out the math so plainly even Troy Jackson should be able to understand it. In that year, they were paid $369.6 million to provide $542.4 million in services, which comes out to a $172 million loss.
In the previous year, [MaineHealth's MaineCare losses](https://substack.com/redirect/1d208e4b-4c7d-42e1-8dfa-3284f21189ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) were just $82.4 million.
The Northern Light hospital system [reports](https://substack.com/redirect/c9eba25f-45b6-40bb-bf62-ef1fe8ba3062?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) similar losses to treat the expanded Medicaid population. For just the Eastern Maine Medical Center (EMMC) facility, the hospital operator reports losing $80 million to treat MaineCare patients.
The evidence is clear: Maine's hospitals lose money when they provide care to MaineCare members. That's because the reimbursement rates under MaineCare are less than what healthcare services cost to provide. It therefore follows that when the class of patients relying on MaineCare grows, Maine's hospitals will lose more money. When a business loses money year after year, and loses it at an accelerating rate, that business has to stop offering non-profitable services or it will soon be altogether bankrupt. The hospitals can paper over losses with ad hoc government grants -- and by jacking up prices for the commercially insured -- but that's not sustainable when Medicaid rolls continue to swell. That's especially the case when the Medicaid rolls swell unpredictably with the sudden arrival of thousands of jobless, homeless migrants.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..ccZ7vLZLJ19DZTVab3bqS-zFZpHOWNJZBZ1vbJfZOaE?)
From 2010 to 2024, MaineHealth's Medicaid losses rose by 4.4x, while Northern Light's (and its predecessor's) more than doubled. Eventually, our state's healthcare system reaches the tipping point where the population of takers is too big for the population of makers to support. Expanding a below-cost payer population without expanding medical supply or adequately financing the resulting care may be free for the patient, but it's not free for the hospital or the taxpayer. The cost is shifted to commercial premiums, taxpayers, delayed investment, longer waits for care, eliminated services, staff vacancies, and, eventually, closed doors.
Medicaid expansion is especially damaging to hospitals when it comes to pregnancies because childbirth is among the most common and expensive major services. That's precisely what's happening with Maine's rural hospitals and the maternity wards. Maine's extremely low birth rates, especially in Lincoln County, have certainly undermined the business model of the birthing center in that area. But MaineCare has undoubtedly played a role, too.
If you're a Maine couple looking to start a family, you can expect to pay $20,000-$35,000 for a stay in the maternity ward. Maybe, if you're lucky, you've hit your deductible or your out-of-pocket max. However, if you're a jobless, unwed father working under the table at a weed farm, or an illegal alien from Central Africa who arrived in Maine in 2022, you can buy snacks at the cafeteria with your EBT card while your procreation partner gives birth at a cost to you of zero dollars. Data from the Maine Health Data Organization (MHDO) shows that 40 percent of births are covered under MaineCare, which means that birthing centers aren't getting fair pay for almost half of all pregnancies. The low reimbursement rate combined with the low birth rate is the perfect storm to render rural birth centers economically unsustainable to operate.
That same reasoning goes for every other health care service offered in Maine. MHDO data shows the specific details of the losses medical providers bear when treating the welfare class. The reported average payment was dramatically lower for welfare patients versus working patients. The [dashboard](https://substack.com/redirect/49028f02-47e3-4ed8-bc7c-e80b24107c26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows approximately $2,430 per MaineCare inpatient unit compared with $8,728 commercially, and about $334 per MaineCare emergency-room unit compared with $1,279 commercially. To avoid confusion, the reader should understand that those MaineCare costs are paid by taxpayers to the medical provider, while the private payor cost figures come from commercial insurers, like employer-sponsored plans. The non-working, non-citizen classes get everything for free, while the working class gets to pick up the increasingly sky-high tab.
But wait, there's more! Because the paltry reimbursement rate isn't the only way Medicaid expansion harmed Maine's medical industry.
Democrats' Medicaid expansion didn't just force hospitals to lose money treating a larger population of welfare recipients. It also forced them to treat those non-paying patients more often than people who work for a living, who have Medicare benefits they paid for while they were working, or who otherwise pay their own way. That's because individuals who get free care through Medicaid are far more likely to visit the doctor or pop into the emergency room than those with private insurance.
The Maine Health Data Organization's (MHDO) All-Payer Claims Database shows the sharp differences between the MaineCare population and the co-pay population when it comes to going to the doctor's office or the hospital. According to the MHDO data for 2024, there were 238 inpatient admissions per 1,000 MaineCare members, compared with 102 per 1,000 commercially insured people. MaineCare hospital-outpatient utilization was about 50 percent higher for the commercially insured. Emergency-room utilization was approximately 325 visits per 1,000 MaineCare members, more than twice the commercial rate of 161 per 1,000. In other words, the Mainers (and noncitizens) who are on welfare are consuming medical services at more than DOUBLE the rate of Mainers with co-pays and deductibles.

Perhaps this helps you understand why the emergency rooms are always clogged with people who appear to be mentally ill demanding trauma surgeons for their bloody noses or an MRI for their hangnail. In fairness, some of that utilization difference reflects poorer health, disability, behavioral-health needs, and different demographic characteristics for lower-income MaineCare members. But it also reflects the basic human behavior to take advantage of "free" stuff when you have no skin in the game at all. But regardless of the cause, the over-utilization of healthcare caused by Medicaid expansion exacerbated pre-existing staffing issues. Twice the emergency-room demand remains twice the demand, and more nurses and doctors don't magically appear just because the line at the door has doubled in length.
But wait, there's more! We have barely covered the list of Democratic policies that have harmed Maine's medical providers!
Janet Mills' draconian Covid-19 policies added new costs to Maine's hospitals by forcing them to hire costly travel nurses. Both Northern Light and MaineHealth reported substantial costs paid to out-of-state travel nurse agencies because healthcare workers were forced out of their jobs by the governor's immoral vaccine mandates. Mills' unilateral decision to usurp healthcare workers' bodily autonomy for the sake of a now-discredited experimental mRNA therapy created a healthcare worker shortage in the middle of a healthcare crisis. Both of the big hospital systems reported massive outlays to bring in out-of-state workers.
Not Just Predictable -- Predicted!
Medicaid expansion -- the crowning achievement of the Maine Democratic Party over the last 10 years -- destroyed healthcare in Maine. Is the emergency room overrun when you're trying to get your kid seen for strep throat or a broken wrist? Blame Medicaid expansion. Have your commercial insurance costs doubled in the last decade? Blame Medicaid expansion. Are you worried about rural hospitals closing? Well, guess what's to blame: Medicaid expansion. All of these deleterious consequences weren't just predictable -- they were predicted -- predicted by former Gov. Paul LePage, who's now running for Maine's open Second Congressional District.
LePage warned like Jeremiah that expanding MaineCare would wreck the state budget while doing nothing to improve the lives of poor and working-class Mainers -- and he was right.
Now, the same people who shrieked for more than a decade that more MaineCare was the cure-all for all of Maine's problems are trying to distract from the corrosive failures of their previous policies by bleating about "Medicare for All."
Newsflash: "Medicare for All" is the exact same policy -- but worse.
As the old George W. Bush saying goes, "Fool me once, shame on -- shame on you. Fool me -- you can't get fooled again."
So what can the people of Maine do to avoid getting fooled again by the billionaire-funded politicians like Hannah Pingree, Troy Jackson, and the Democratic rent-a-mob?
For starters, let's look at the evidence and the facts.
Let's insist on evidence-based policies.
Because we have eight years of data showing what happens when far-left DSA Democrats get their policy wish list rammed through Augusta. And if voters or lawmakers rely on the evidence and objective facts, they will see that Medicaid expansion has been ruinous for our hospitals without measurably improving healthcare outcomes for Mainers.
Rather than make Mainers healthier, Medicaid expansion created the perverse incentives that are destroying the medical industry in Maine. Medicare for All would make all the same mistakes, but worse.

Twice the emergency-room demand remains twice the demand, and more nurses and doctors don't magically appear just because the line at the door has doubled in length. But wait, there's more! We have barely covered the list of Democratic policies that have harmed Maine's medical providers! Janet Mills' draconian Covid-19 policies added new costs to Maine's hospitals by forcing them to hire costly travel nurses. Both Northern Light and MaineHealth reported substantial costs paid to out-of-state travel nurse agencies because healthcare workers were forced out of their jobs by the governor's immoral vaccine mandates. Mills' unilateral decision to usurp healthcare workers' bodily autonomy for the sake of a now-discredited experimental mRNA therapy created a healthcare worker shortage in the middle of a healthcare crisis. Both of the big hospital systems reported massive outlays to bring in out-of-state workers. Not Just Predictable -- Predicted! Medicaid expansion -- the crowning achievement of the Maine Democratic Party over the last 10 years -- destroyed healthcare in Maine. Is the emergency room overrun when you're trying to get your kid seen for strep throat or a broken wrist? Blame Medicaid expansion. Have your commercial insurance costs doubled in the last decade? Blame Medicaid expansion. Are you worried about rural hospitals closing? Well, guess what's to blame: Medicaid expansion. All of these deleterious consequences weren't just predictable -- they were predicted -- predicted by former Gov. Paul LePage, who's now running for Maine's open Second Congressional District. LePage warned like Jeremiah that expanding MaineCare would wreck the state budget while doing nothing to improve the lives of poor and working-class Mainers -- and he was right. Now, the same people who shrieked for more than a decade that more MaineCare was the cure-all for all of Maine's problems are trying to distract from the corrosive failures of their previous policies by bleating about "Medicare for All." Newsflash: "Medicare for All" is the exact same policy -- but worse. As the old George W. Bush saying goes, "Fool me once, shame on -- shame on you. Fool me -- you can't get fooled again." So what can the people of Maine do to avoid getting fooled again by the billionaire-funded politicians like Hannah Pingree, Troy Jackson, and the Democratic rent-a-mob? For starters, let's look at the evidence and the facts. Let's insist on evidence-based policies. Because we have eight years of data showing what happens when far-left DSA Democrats get their policy wish list rammed through Augusta. And if voters or lawmakers rely on the evidence and objective facts, they will see that Medicaid expansion has been ruinous for our hospitals without measurably improving healthcare outcomes for Mainers. Rather than make Mainers healthier, Medicaid expansion created the perverse incentives that are destroying the medical industry in Maine. Medicare for All would make all the same mistakes, but worse. ? * You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. Haitians living in the United States are officially on notice after their Temporary Protected Status was allowed to expire following lengthy court battles.
As usual when it comes to immigration policies from the Trump administration, immigration advocates say ending TPS for Haitians is cruel and unfair because Haiti is still embroiled in violence and does not have a stable government. Haitians were initially given TPS after the 2010 earthquake.
The Left's arguments would have merit had they not glossed over what took place during the Biden-Harris administration. It should be no surprise that Haitians were among the nationalities that were illegally crossing the U.S.-Mexico border under Joe Biden.
In my experience, I saw hundreds of Haitians crossing into Yuma, Arizona when that region started seeing a spike in encounters. The most infamous episode was when tens of thousands of Haitians flooded into Del Rio, Texas, camping under the international bridge while waiting to be processed and released into our country.
The big question everyone at that time was asking was how could these people be coming from Haiti if they were improvised and flights were not readily available due to the widespread gang violence?

## _Chip In Today To Help Us Get Out The Vote!_

**Friends,**
**Good news: This is (hopefully) the last campaign fundraising email you'll get from us before Election Day. Take a moment. Soak it in. Tell your inbox we said you're welcome.****...****Well, it’s the last email until the General Election! This is actually the last campaign fundraising email before **_**this**_** election.**
**Now that we've cleared up that technicality, here's why we're asking one last time: Tomorrow is Election Day, and it’s all about one thing: getting out the vote.**
**We're knocking doors, making phone calls, talking to neighbors, putting up signs, talking to every last voter, and making sure supporters make it to the polls. Every dollar helps us build momentum, fuel volunteers, and keep our team out in the community from sunup until the polls close.**
**If you've been waiting for the right moment to chip in, this is it. Whether it's $10, $25, or whatever you can spare, your contribution today goes directly toward our final push to reach voters before they cast their ballots.**
**This campaign has always been powered by neighbors who believe our community deserves strong, local leadership. We're incredibly grateful for every volunteer, every conversation, every vote, and every donation.**
**If you can, please chip in today and help us finish strong.**
**Thank you for sticking with us through all the emails, all the updates, and all the campaign excitement. With your help, we'll make tomorrow count.**
**-Elizabeth**

Peter,

I want to take a minute to say thank you.

Not only to those who chipped in toward our deadline push, but to everyone who's been opening and reading these emails -- even when you haven't been able to give.

That matters more than you might think. Every time you open one of our notes, it tells email providers that people actually want to hear from us -- which helps us reach more inboxes and supporters. So even just being here and paying attention is doing something for this campaign.

Today, I'm not asking you for money.

I'm asking something smaller, but it means a lot to me personally: will you add your name to endorse this campaign?

Friends [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50] , Election Day is officially right around the corner — exactly 3 months to go.
So let’s talk about something important that’s been on my mind: the outcomes of the midterm elections are not a foregone conclusion.
I know it can feel that way when we all read the news and listen to podcasts. We see the breakdown of the Senate map and the path to flipping the House, look at all the polls, and hear about the likelihood of winning or losing certain seats. In this media environment, with confident forecasts flying left and right (and people quite literally betting on our elections using prediction markets), it’s easy to start to believe certain outcomes are already in the bag.
But I want to remind you that that’s simply not the case. Quite the opposite:
What happens in November completely depends on what WE do over the next 92 days!
Whether you feel like a race is hopelessly lost to an extreme MAGA Republican, or a candidate is a sure bet in a blue district, the reality is that neither of those things is true .
The news we’ll wake up to on November 3rd rests in our hands, and the measures we take between now and then have real power.
Today, I’m asking you to take action to help ensure the outcomes we’re fighting for. We *can* defeat MAGA extremists, we *can* flip the House and take back the Senate, and we *can* hold this administration accountable while working to deliver real solutions for the American people. But we won’t get it done if we don’t put in the work.
Will you chip in any amount – whether that’s $5, $20, or $30 – to help make it happen? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]

Folks, I spent my Friday doing something I highly recommend: sitting down with our partners at Defiance.org to count the week's MAGA losses out loud, on their show, as their guest. And what a list it was. A twenty-year-old named Ryland Ferguson stole an entire Trump rally in Georgia by delivering--directly over the man's shoulder, on camera--what I'll generously call an homage. Alan Ritchson, who plays Reacher himself, went on a righteous, gloriously profane tear demanding the Epstein files--go find the clip, I'll wait. John Thune told Karoline Leavitt that if passing Trump's stalled bill is so easy, she can get on the phone and find the votes herself. And Mike Lindell--the loudest "election integrity" crusader in America--spent the week answering some very interesting questions about his own voter registration in the state where he's running for governor.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.9HMfXlvbmXufiWYb_MtBxqIoPFUkmo7uYznkhf_TNV4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209690302)
But the loss that matters most is the one with a bank statement attached. Citizens Bank announced it will stop financing GEO Group and CoreCivic--the two private prison giants behind Trump's detention camps--after New Jersey city councils voted to pull their deposits and ordinary citizens ran a pressure campaign that made the business untenable. Nobody at that bank suddenly grew a conscience. They reacted to you. That's the thing I keep saying on every show that will have me: courage is contagious, and institutions respond to markets and to shame. The actor finds his spine, the senator talks back, the bank divests--because millions of people made standing with democracy popular and standing with the would-be king expensive.
_**That 's exactly why Blue Amp Media partnered with Defiance**_. The other side spent fifty years building its machine; we're building ours, and it runs on two engines. The media engine is this newsletter and our shows--**[so subscribe to Blue Amp Media, free or paid, and bring a friend, because every subscriber makes us louder and harder to ignore](https://substack.com/redirect/464fef24-59af-42a6-b862-111e293c98f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. The action engine is Defiance: a member-funded club that has taken a concrete action against Trump's corruption every single week since it launched--lawsuits, prosecutors holding lawless federal agents accountable, election protection before agents ever reach a polling place--with most of the money going right back out the door to the front lines. Watch the full episode above, then do both things. That's how this works: a bigger media network, a bigger resistance network, and you in both.

clean_body: Everything I do is to support the nation that has given me so much. | Fellow Conservative, We have less than 100 days until Election Day - and our Primary election is less than 2 weeks away. We are entering the most critical part of our mission to flip this open seat in Minnesota - and I need to know you're on my team. Everything I do is to support the nation that has given me so much. I am a born-and-raised Minnesotan, a values-driven, unapologetic American enthusiast, and a battle-tested warrior. I deployed 9 times to keep America safe, first as a Marine, then as a Navy SEAL. Now, I'm running for the U.S. Senate to represent the people of Minnesota because they deserve strong, principled leadership that will jump-start the economy, make the government accountable, instill conservative values, and put our national security first. But I cannot do this alone. I need folks just like you to step up and join our grassroots movement if we want to win in November. toward helping us not only win on August 11 but also defeat the Democrat machine that's gone unchecked for far too long in Minnesota. Fraud, corruption, and special interests run our state. It's time to change that. Now more than ever, America needs real leaders in Washington. Leaders who can't be bought by special interests. Leaders who know how to fight and win. Thank you, Adam Schwarze Former Navy SEAL Minnesota Republican Party Endorsed Candidate for U.S. Senate FOLLOW ADAM ON SOCIAL MEDIA | | Paid for by Schwarze for Senate Adam Schwarze is a former Navy SEAL and Marine. body:
The difference between the rule of law and a surveillance state. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqGxyh2qvWlDF4gTB51TOhmhUYsxJ9dpr_F3qbom3vj7JXkfwanGfF6ljgokH3zTObwOdl4V5bFxtLZ5zb0alqm5-XFTJpdvOzXCeUXUJFOAugouh7ZJsp0MltDEoZjXa7amVfzQC5W4nr5npt8KTZlps3kp4VeSMs2C1suru2leJvQ_8hvA45esHYdFjFb-22YIPYWA5-9vM7NiToqmlUbKw/4sv/4owCLYLhQPG0RDD-bNw7Sw/h0/h001.3TTLc3BpVCDH-Jaoac6SQSvanaVK4gPU8Zy1JIroYFI)
---
Peter, All across our district, communities are quietly putting up **Flock cameras.** Right here in McKinney, the city council approved 13 of them along the major highways. They photograph every car that passes, log your plate along with the make, model, color, time, and location, and feed it all into a database that police can search whenever they want. Used the right way, on kidnappings and human trafficking and violent crime, that can save lives. I have no problem with that. **What keeps me up at night is everything that happens when a tool like this slips its leash, because it always does.**
---
[ **No surveillance state in Texas.** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8_OPMKR7Eiurhk7IAHW9UhGyMTgvmQzNegXNQGGqMh30OowJzzKD4ezsVJ2qpXdeOv8toINydHgsQZJ3TBO5JJ8dzHHZxaKvyXkkwz5GlFIROPRM7hLtZ2pWOiJSHVw9aKOwcqySFVeiC5-eDSSkjrHrtnSYipr2eZ_U4SvwlrI4MMBFANSVezsvHrgNJ-UL5Lg5Ct7G12D58frf3Ar3d0k7IlqBkS6hZnB55Oaaw-KXriGTvQqUxxy2p-JtHUJ0BUFgeu5ObOAZvA_c--PBTb6wwQAywuwieAEmb3NlmbGv-JHPT5g_fQTaH993-7HQmKMFDu-9_8Q26tL-voB04FJjHDnM2c8e7d3Nv1U-fZjY/4sv/4owCLYLhQPG0RDD-bNw7Sw/h1/h001.sHujKieh3Jd7AmiGfreXa6UWQ5dJVg03eJ6KqaU_y1Y)
---
Last year, investigators used a network of more than 83,000 of these cameras to track down a woman after she had a self-managed abortion. They called it a welfare check but court records later showed they were weighing criminal charges. Around the country, police officers have been caught using these same systems to **stalk their ex-girlfriends and former wives**. And many times, these cameras are not even good at their actual job. In one California town, **71% of the alerts Flock sent police turned out to be misreads** , flagging innocent people as driving stolen or felony vehicles. [**Help us send someone to Congress who will rein this technology in before it becomes a permanent tool for stalking and control.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8_OPMKR7Eiurhk7IAHW9UhFfduRvIo2wEuqVuzTmqDOYOJHF_fK8oQo0BOhDd77j53-kRt1CAYz9eZKmaFZOj_M9-gRwqG-ImW6jY9KOZeRaaLL7eunMm9RQ_Yj-A4zVLHbm2_liHA5Dwsmde3g0hEBUcf84mqvcnrYmcv0P0MpF_0mPbxKjDkaV3Qq22DSfxi0cTCJW_VMVSCsjPLuiiuZ-E07S3nQ-okQUu4cDfv3CQ7dWe5B0GQ7D5Qiwewm2N-cbuIzO1nM1_byox58AUtW4dFHP9ZpIc4R6-5Rx4HaGHgN1RLsAt67YE1Xlf0N5MQ0l3cyBQwE3HvcisIIYrg2kuLS190k1GJFexamRnFYi/4sv/4owCLYLhQPG0RDD-bNw7Sw/h2/h001.LAnvg035_R1066JxpjH383pxowujwJXR-8txMCrcEvA) With advancements in AI, these systems can now stitch together millions of data points in seconds and build a detailed map of where you live, work, worship, see your doctor, and show up to speak your mind. **That is the machinery of a surveillance state, and we are bolting it up on our own highways without a serious conversation about the guardrails.** Keith Self has introduced a bill requiring federal agents to get a warrant before tapping these systems and that is a fine first step. But it is nowhere near enough. It says nothing about AI, nothing about the data brokers buying and selling your travel history, and nothing about privacy protections. I spent 20 years in uniform but the oath I swore to uphold and defend our Constitution did not end when I retired. I will not stand while this country turns into an overwatch state. [**Help us flip this seat and go build the guardrails while we still can.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8_OPMKR7Eiurhk7IAHW9UhFhY2QRJ_NX2_irMHf1MwLZHrYBEBKZY71XHPOPoZdIR8fo_b36PP7zmMIBAWR6dUOKfwLlGapGc5ZG-m3AFyQ89wH2NJxrZGgigIgzYlPEkFWeCFFOHjfxemfpGPBPz8FboAqteuDZI9ol4WdvI_ZqryNFfnJpDl-3QQnXMPKi1FsfSz1U0IgtkL3YBzqa-Ph_RY8Qsi6oMPQRYvjKBJ9kw5cAS2Z-ZiErc8KOkQ4AVAUm911P13fmf1yQ5DdfAm3t6E6gSHenc48MXGt2MuFzgWI7F8XinJqNvgEPeIEeY-s19XuAcCeemSCKwosN2zrA2MOFmBJ0L-ZCI0aUN38H/4sv/4owCLYLhQPG0RDD-bNw7Sw/h3/h001.iR5BUewHRssKrhkfIqS22DUGzTxJXyMv6s42mNjxBOg) Very respectfully, Evan Hunt Democratic Nominee TX-03

clean_body: The difference between the rule of law and a surveillance state. | | Peter, All across our district, communities are quietly putting up Flock cameras. Right here in McKinney, the city council approved 13 of them along the major highways. They photograph every car that passes, log your plate along with the make, model, color, time, and location, and feed it all into a database that police can search whenever they want. Used the right way, on kidnappings and human trafficking and violent crime, that can save lives. I have no problem with that. What keeps me up at night is everything that happens when a tool like this slips its leash, because it always does. Last year, investigators used a network of more than 83,000 of these cameras to track down a woman after she had a self-managed abortion. They called it a welfare check but court records later showed they were weighing criminal charges. Around the country, police officers have been caught using these same systems to stalk their ex-girlfriends and former wives. And many times, these cameras are not even good at their actual job. In one California town, 71% of the alerts Flock sent police turned out to be misreads , flagging innocent people as driving stolen or felony vehicles. With advancements in AI, these systems can now stitch together millions of data points in seconds and build a detailed map of where you live, work, worship, see your doctor, and show up to speak your mind. That is the machinery of a surveillance state, and we are bolting it up on our own highways without a serious conversation about the guardrails. Keith Self has introduced a bill requiring federal agents to get a warrant before tapping these systems and that is a fine first step. But it is nowhere near enough. It says nothing about AI, nothing about the data brokers buying and selling your travel history, and nothing about privacy protections. I spent 20 years in uniform but the oath I swore to uphold and defend our Constitution did not end when I retired. I will not stand while this country turns into an overwatch state. I am the only lung and critical care doctor in Congress.
That means that I, unlike most of my colleagues, have seen exactly what a bad wildfire season means for the health and safety of our communities.
Right now, more than two million acres of Oregon land are on fire. Animals are losing their habitat, farmers are losing their grazing land, and Oregonians are losing their homes. I will not stand on the sidelines while D.C. insiders put profit over our families and let our states burn.
I introduced the Climate Health Emergency Act to finally unlock federal resources to combat this crisis as the public health emergency it is.
Wildfire seasons are increasingly intense and long. Our youth are growing up on a planet that's more stressed and less resilient, undermining their hope for their futures. We don’t have to accept this reality.
I will relentlessly fight to protect our environment, center science in our decisions, and put my constituents first. Hi, winning this Senate race just got a lot harder.

name: Dave Beckwith for Congress
subject: Tomorrow decides it. Here's everything I'm fighting for.
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Dave Beckwith For Congress_
body:
| | | | Hi Friend,
Tomorrow is Election Day in VA-10, and I wanted to reach you tonight, before the polls open, to remind you exactly what this campaign has been about from day one.
I didn't get into this race to be a career politician. I spent 30 years in the Air Force, rose to Colonel, and oversaw a $500 billion national security portfolio at the Pentagon as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense. I've lived in Loudoun County for 17 years as your neighbor. I'm a homeschool dad, a cancer survivor, and I've been married for over 30 years. I know what families in this district are up against, because I'm living it too.
Every policy I'm running on answers one question: _**what's standing between the people of VA-10 and their American Dream, and how do we remove it?**_ Here's exactly what that means:
**Restoring Economic Vitality** I'll fight to keep taxes low with my plan to implement a 5% tax rate for earners under $200,000. I'll work to unlock the housing market by pushing for portable mortgages and indexing capital gains to inflation. I'll always support cutting burdensome regulations, and pursue an all-of-the-above energy strategy that lowers costs for families and small businesses. Washington shouldn't make it harder to build a life here, nor should it ever take more from hardworking families than it needs.
**Fiscal Responsibility** Washington should live by the same rule your family does: don't spend more than you take in. I'll be a steadfast voice for eliminating wasteful spending and combating the fraud that costs taxpayers up to $521 billion every year. We have a moral obligation to the next generation to hand them a country full of opportunity, not a $40 trillion debt they had no part in creating.
**Safety and Security in Our Communities** I'm a staunch supporter of law enforcement, because well-resourced police departments make safer neighborhoods. Your family's safety isn't negotiable, and I'll make sure Washington treats it that way.
**Upholding Our 2nd Amendment Rights** I'll defend the constitutional right to bear arms for every law-abiding citizen. Personal safety is a fundamental right, not a privilege the government hands out. Beyond the 2nd Amendment, the Constitution isn't something you can pick and choose from when it's politically convenient. Before I cast any vote in Congress, I'll ask myself "does this uphold or undermine the Constitutional rights of the people I represent?"
**Releasing American Energy** I support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that ends market-distorting subsidies and unleashes American innovation, including a bold reinvestment in nuclear power to lower energy costs and create good jobs. VA-10 families shouldn't be stuck footing the bill for a grid that's struggling to keep pace with demand.
**Education for Our Modern Economy** I'll advocate for parental rights and school choice, and work to expand access to vocational training and apprenticeships, so every student has a real path to a high-paying career, instead of treating a college degree as the only option.
**Supporting Our Veterans** I'll fight for the men and women who defended this country, so they get timely healthcare, real support for their mental health, and the benefits they earned without the bureaucratic runaround.

_**But none of this happens unless you vote.**_ Polls are open tomorrow, Tuesday, August 4th, from 6am to 7pm. If you haven't voted yet, tomorrow is your last chance to make your voice heard in this election.
Find your polling place here: [www.elections.virginia.gov/casting-a-ballot/polling-place-lookup/](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)

I've spent my life in service to this country and this community. Now I'm asking for your vote so I can bring that same service to Congress and fight for VA-10's American Dream. Thank you for standing with me.
---
| | | God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

body:
Peter, I'm retiring from Congress, and I honestly expected more.
I'm not angry, I'm just disappointed. A few days ago, I sent out the signal calling on every conservative patriot in the nation to help me secure my legacy and rescue this seat from the Democrat vultures.
But nothing happened.
No cavalry came. As I prepare to step down, it felt like I was left to fight the entire Democratic Party by myself. For a moment, I actually feared for the future of the MAGA movement.
But then I remembered, YOU never let us down, Peter. You are the reason for our historic victories, and I know you would never turn your back on this movement, especially now that I am passing the torch to the next generation.

Hey folks,
The panic inside MAGA is getting a whole lot louder--and for the first time in a long time, it might actually be justified.
CNN's Harry Enten just laid out why Texas isn't following the old playbook anymore, and the numbers are hard to ignore. James Talarico is leading in multiple high-quality polls, independent voters are breaking hard against Republicans, and suddenly the state Republicans always assumed was untouchable is looking like the biggest battleground in the country.
If Texas flips, it doesn't just change one Senate seat. It changes everything.
* **00:01:13** Harry Enten explains why this is the strongest polling Democrats have seen in a Texas Senate race in decades--and why this year looks different.
* **00:03:30** We break down why Ken Paxton's weaknesses and Talarico's strengths are creating an opening Republicans never expected.
* **00:05:20** Trump's collapsing support with independent voters could reshape Senate races far beyond Texas.
* **00:07:38** Trump's reaction to the polling says a lot--and raises serious questions about how he'll respond if Republicans lose in November.
* **00:10:46** We zoom out to the national map and why multiple Senate races are showing the same trend: Democrats polling above 50% in states that once seemed out of reach.

This episode isn't just about one race in Texas. It's about what happens when the political landscape starts shifting underneath everyone's feet. We talk through the polling, what it actually means, why independent voters matter so much right now, and why none of this is a reason to get complacent. If the numbers hold, Democrats have a real opportunity--but only if people stay engaged and keep organizing until the last vote is counted.

There are 92 days until the midterm general elections. Primaries have already started. State legislative sessions are in full swing, with more right around the corner, and suppressive bills are on the rise again.
What does this all mean? Our work is going full speed right now , not waiting for the summer. The foundation we lay right now is what sets the stage for November's elections.
RUSH $35 or more right now and help make every vote count and every voice heard in our elections nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=080326_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
The Atlantic: Donald Trump’s Plan to Subvert the Midterms Is Already Under Way [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=080326_3&amount=25]
Team, that headline from The Atlantic says it all.
Donald Trump already promised as part of his 2024 campaign that “ we’ll have it fixed so good, you’re not gonna have to vote .” Watching his actions after he lost in 2020 -- lies, denial, rallies, all leading to January 6th -- it's not hard to imagine what he's got in mind for November.
Our states run our elections. But that doesn't mean that MAGA-aligned politicians won't follow his illegal orders to interfere. It doesn't stop him from using ICE agents to intimidate at the polls or threaten eligible voters. And it doesn't stop his Department of Justice from trying to interfere through the courts, especially when more than half of the suppressive lawsuits brought to court this year were brought by the very federal department that's supposed to protect our rights.
None of that takes into account the highly partisan efforts for mid-decade redistricting as well. It's clear that the threats to the next election aren't going to stop. That's where we come in.
We must inform voters, defend our elections, and make sure every eligible vote counts. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to fuel our voting rights work for 2026 and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=080326_3&amount=35]

Our democracy, our elections, and our fundamental right to vote have been under attack for more than a decade. Our electoral system is reaching a breaking point, and it's hard to predict exactly where the next set of electoral shenanigans will come from.
Are we destined to watch our elections break down? Absolutely not. We still have the time and the people to win. What we need most is the resources to carry on this fight for our democracy and the work to make every voice heard in our elections.
Stopping their attempts to subvert the midterms will require courage and integrity across the board. Most of all, it will depend on individual Americans like us to stand up for our rights and demand that our votes are counted.
This is a fight we can and will win. Stand with us to protect the right to vote by pitching in with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=080326_3&amount=35]

When Republicans redrew this district to make it more politically friendly to the GOP, many political insiders counted us out. But because of supporters like you, we've built a campaign that is proving we're ready to compete. | | Peter Willis, **Tomorrow is our primary election.**

It's important because we not only get to nominate our candidates for the general election, but this year we can change how the Kansas Supreme Court is selected.

It's currently a lawyer-dominated commission and Kansans have no voice on who sits on our Supreme Court.

**I encourage you to vote YES on the Right to Vote Amendment. Vote YES to give Kansans a say on who serves on our state's highest court. **

Currently, 8 of the 9 members of the current Supreme Court nominating commission are Democrat donors.

This system is why our Kansas Supreme Court is so liberal and to the left of rural Kansas, making terrible ruling after terrible ruling.

We can trust Kansans to vote on these critical matters. Vote YES on the Constitutional Amendment to elect our judges.

You can find your polling location [here](https://kansasvoterinfo.gov/VoterView).

Together, as Republicans, we'll continue fighting for the values that built this country and ensure the next generation inherits an America that is stronger, freer, and more prosperous than ever before.

Yours in the fight,

Tracey Mann

We have built this campaign over more than a year with thousands of grassroots donations, and I am so honored to know that this Team has my back. **Together, we will win tomorrow – and then take the fight directly to Tom Barrett.** I’m running for Congress not because this was ever part of some big life plan. But because I swore an oath to the Constitution and I fought for it for 20 years, and I feel like I’m watching Trump rip that Constitution up in front of my eyes everyday. We cannot let this happen. Not on our watch. For 250 years, our country has endured some of its darkest chapters because ordinary people chose to live with courage. [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/120031/images/eon%20header.png]
I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch. Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.
Will you chip in $10, $20, or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now and Resist Reclaim Rebuild today to help us elect leaders who won't be intimidated — no matter what they face? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon] [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
CHIP IN TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-eon]
They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi

Trump Halts Iran Strike
President Trump called off what he described as the largest planned U.S. military operation since World War II, [saying Gulf allies](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckDuynDAQAE8jMlFCiEUbKHBC9pw6pIQ0hvHTrzTDvrJP79rIuS_Q1d0_PvYPjwnL-d1ncEi0xxr37HP0BemsL-glQ-F-l7PXsGulH1JZqebdB8YX7MYP0S16sj_tAG5a7WLVpK0dLjcd8xxgMnNYjwm0XZ9qsqsCvSqzxLgM6N48ZdWs58WYdYzR2ON5qIcyz8UYI4y6W_QMIxbCCBRqba0mZAw01n4OyV3MjcT8TehN6O3XTcwXFPiiMdQs9PYvQuiNINwd-bfQG_c7Nxl8SiQ9sw-fErsvMiBjOWXr9exAJCP4JGuDIom7R5ZX7fn-I32JEkqU5f4EGrqL7QtTQnqswqgze0xvgYH_9-rL6b8BAAD__75FjJo) and Tehran had asked for time to finish a deal. The emerging framework promises the "Immediate, Complete, and Total" [reopening of Hormuz](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2OrSAUQOGngQ6DCIgFxW3szm2nNFvheHbCjwHUyTz9xFeYcjVfsb5eywswYNr_Q_QWa11cdkuE6CBh3fPlS4o-tXKmveRtEVxoxg3jwwJbw8svEqizSvTmbai3_WiU4b0whn4saKFAelj1qofJKTUNTsnRK83fvZcbRft43PBBDErKsXNOmnVaueZyUlJKIvl5OGi-w1TR-brlfBw5YMOtdrnsNNhPa0clwz8iZiLm-767d_5O_q7dliMRc8DLs6eJmFs548GwQGI3FIa1gA_sk0s8fxic-1kbE7RYd9wYAlY9Esn3CBgejLa_Hrqs-A0AAP__ENB47g) and an end to Iran's nuclear program, with negotiations set to begin Monday afternoon. Returning from Bedminster, Trump told reporters the request came from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, and [Iran itself](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2SpSAUQOHVYIaFV1QMCCYxe5NOaCFcfbeGHwdQp3ff9bbQGzin6vvzWl-GPMXjtwmoqZTVJbcGE5yJVI50Y44BY81XPHKyKwgYuVBc9KuxlW5cpWmcHqBTu2pQd5MalOhAqeate6vULIZOKduJrsdtm2YY5WjBOueEaUh_ekKJHvpByql1Tqpt3sQo5DxIKZkU1-lMxZZiIYfFpnSeyVMlW9qUj8brd61nYf0vBguD5Xme9jHlTfGoKeJ_Eyhibm0KDBZnyH_xFLnDHWNBBoscJ5AdMFhqvsLJrfEeHU_7zp-HiHu80fNSM_1FnvHfhaXy4_I7N94TFk7ZRAZLk7U7H_KeyjgxKY5gyH-2Tf0p663hOwAA__9wPor8). Hawks in both parties fear Tehran is stalling yet again, but the White House is betting maximum pressure finally cracked the regime. ★★★
